2.5 Discretization Semantics Disc
Disc defines how the generator becomes a step map E∆t.

597



Disc Component (required)

Disc := (StepType, ∆t, Schedule, Order, RoundingPolicy, StopRule).

Rule. Disc MUST be fully explicit. ∆t and the schedule (number of steps, time horizon) MUST
be fixed or derived deterministically from committed public inputs.

Allowed Step Types (Baseline Set)

EY25 permits at minimum:
• D1: Euler (first order): ρn+1 = ρn + ∆tL(ρn)
• D2: RK2 / midpoint (second order) with explicit formula and fixed evaluation order
• D3: Trotter product for commutator generators with fixed factorization rule

Normative note. Higher-order integrators MAY be defined by future profiles, but must remain
deterministic and transcript-replayable.

2.6 Truncation Semantics Trunc
Trunc binds how infinite objects are represented finitely for verification.

Trunc Component (required).
Trunc := (Basis, CutRule, BoundaryRule, {Nℓ}, CrossNPolicy).

This reuses EY22 truncation vocabulary.

Rule. If truncation is used, the required truncation levels {Nℓ} MUST be fixed in SpecID and
MUST be used consistently for transcript commitments.

2.7 Transcript Contract

Audit-native evolution requires publishing a transcript commitment.

Transcript. A transcript is an ordered sequence of scalar commitments (or hashes) that bind
the evolution: ( )

Tx := Tx0,Tx1, . . . ,TxT ,

where each Txn commits to the state/observable representation at step n (or to declared
summaries).

Rule. The SpecID MUST declare what is committed per step:
• full state hash,
• or canonical spectral summaries,
• or bucketed invariants,

and the canonical serialization used.

598



Replay rule. If replay under NumericModel does not reproduce the transcript commitments,
the verifier MUST return FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

2.8 SpecID for EY25

ArtifactType. For EY25:
ArtifactType = LIOUV.

SpecID components (EY25 binding). The full SpecID tuple is:
SpecIDEY25 := (LIOUV, Pic, G, AG, Disc, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Pic (required)

Pic ∈ {state, observable} MUST be declared.

G and AG (required)

G is the generator instance; AG defines the admissible family and membership checks. Even if G
is provided, AG MUST exist to prevent arbitrary hidden generators.

Disc and Trunc (required)

As defined above; fully explicit and deterministic.

TranscriptSpec (required)

TranscriptSpec MUST define:
• what per-step commitments are required,
• the hashing/serialization rules,
• and any permitted compression (e.g. summary-only) and its invariants.

NumericModel (required)

NumericModel MUST include rounding/ordering rules sufficient to make Disc, Trunc, and
transcript commitments deterministic.

Cert, Interop, Version (required)

Cert binds verifier checks; Interop binds compatibility predicates; Version binds meaning and
MUST change if any component changes.

2.9 Deterministic Outcomes

EY25 verification MUST return:
{ACCEPT,REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗},

and MUST support at minimum:

599



• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DISC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_CONSTRAINT

2.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined EY25 as an audit-native evolution artifact: a declared generator family,
explicit discretization semantics, explicit truncation semantics, and a transcript contract for
deterministic replay. It fixed the SpecID binding for EY25 and introduced minimal failure codes.
Chapter 3 next defines admissible generator families AG in detail: canonical parameteriza-
tions, membership checks, controlled dissipation restrictions, and baseline profiles for verifiable
evolution.

3 Admissible Generator Families AG: Canonical Classes for G

3.1 Purpose of AG

The generator specification G is the semantic core of Laudit. If G is underspecified, auditability
collapses: the same name can hide different channel sets, different coupling constants, or different
boundary behavior. Therefore AG is normative: it defines what generator instances are admissible
and how they are encoded and checked.

Rule. A generator G is admissible only if:
• it belongs to a declared generator class,
• it has a canonical parameterization (encoding),
• its parameter bounds are explicit,
• and membership is checkable deterministically under NumericModel.

3.2 Canonical Representation and Encoding

Rule (canonical encoding). Every G ∈ AG MUST have a canonical representation that can
be serialized and compared lexicographically (EY22 Appendix A.1). This canonical encoding
MUST be used by TieBreak whenever a selection rule is enabled in an EY25 profile.

Required encoding fields. The canonical encoding MUST include:
• GenClassID identifying the generator family (G1/G2/G3),
• a parameter tuple θG in a fixed order,
• references (or commitments) to any operators used (e.g. H, V , C, {Lk}),
• explicit bounds and discretization-relevant constants.

600



3.3 Generator Classes

EY25 defines three canonical generator classes. A SpecID MUST select exactly one, or define a
finite union with deterministic tie-break across classes.

Class G1: Commutator (Unitary) Generator

Form.
GG1 := (H), L(ρ) = −i[H, ρ], L∗(g) = i[H, g].

Canonical parameters.

θG1 := (HRef, Pic, UnitsSpec, BoundaryPolicy).

HRef MUST be either:
• a canonical encoding of H in the declared truncation calculus, or
• a hash commitment to the full H object, together with a deterministic truncation map
H 7→ HN .

Membership restrictions.
• H MUST be declared self-adjoint under the chosen AdjointSpec (or an explicit HermitSpec).
• If truncation is used, the sequence HN MUST be deterministically defined.

Use cases. Audit-native unitary evolution and deterministic replay baselines.

Class G2: Lindblad-Like Generator with Controlled Dissipation

Form.
GG2 := (H, {Lk}Kk=1),

∑K (
L(ρ) := −i[H, ρ] + 1 )

LkρL
†
k − 2{L

†
kLk, ρ} .

k=1

Canonical parameters.

θG2 := (HRef, {Lk}Kk=1, K, ChannelOrderRule, DissipationPolicy).

Controlled dissipation policy (normative). DissipationPolicy MUST specify:
• allowed channel families (e.g. local stencils only, sparse-only, validity-derived only),
• allowed target subspaces (a declared projector P or index region),
• and a deterministic bound on total dissipation strength (e.g. ∑k ∥Lk∥2 ≤ BL).

601



Membership restrictions.
• K MUST be finite and bounded: 1 ≤ K ≤ Kmax.
• Each channel Lk MUST belong to a declared admissible family (local/stencil/sparse class)

with explicit bounds.
• Channel ordering MUST be canonical (e.g. lexicographic by encoding), to prevent permu-

tation ambiguity.

Use cases. Audit-native dissipative dynamics with explicit, checkable dissipation channels.

Class G3: Validity-Coupled (Penalty/Audit) Generator

Idea. Couple evolution to validity enforcement as a first-class contract. The generator references
EY24 artifacts and binds to their SpecID.

Canonical instances. EY25 permits two canonical coupling patterns:

(G3a) Hamiltonian augmentation.

H ′ := H + λV, V = C†C,

then use G1 or G2 with H ′.

(G3b) Validity-induced damping channel. Introduce a channel derived from C:

LV := √γ C,

and include LV in the Lindblad channel set.

Canonical parameters.

θG3 := (HRef, EY24Ref, CouplingType ∈ {aug,damp}, λ, γ, OrderRule).

Membership restrictions (normative).
• EY24Ref MUST bind to a full EY24 SpecID and certificate hash (or its canonical commit-

ment).
• Coupling constants λ, γ MUST be bounded and quantized (fixed-point grid) to prevent

tuning smuggling.
• If CouplingType = aug, then addition H + λV MUST be defined in the declared calculus

and truncation policy.
• If CouplingType = damp, then C MUST be admissible under EY24 and channel inclusion

MUST satisfy G2 dissipation bounds.

Use cases. Validity-propagating dynamics where “audit” and “validity” are not external
narratives but generator-level objects.

602



3.4 Parameter Bounds (Anti-Smuggling Requirement)

Rule. Every generator class MUST include explicit bounds sufficient to prevent hidden tuning.
At minimum:

• bounded channel count Kmax (for G2/G3b),
• bounded coupling constants (e.g. λ ∈ [−Λ,Λ], γ ∈ [0,Γ]) on a quantized grid,
• bounded operator magnitudes by declared norm proxy,
• and a finite reference universe for any external IDs (committed by hash if external).

If bounds are omitted, the generator family MUST be treated as non-canonical and verification
MUST reject.

3.5 Baseline Generator Profile (LIOUV-0)

EY25 defines a conservative baseline generator profile intended for universal auditability.

LIOUV-0. Unless overridden, the baseline AG is:

AG,LIOUV-0 := G1 (Commutator Generator)

with:
• explicit HRef encoding or hash commitment with deterministic truncation,
• no dissipation channels,
• and a simple, fully explicit discretization profile (defined in Chapter 4).

Normative note. LIOUV-0 is intentionally conservative: it provides a clean reference baseline
for deterministic replay. Later profiles may enable G2/G3 with controlled dissipation and validity
coupling.

3.6 Membership Check Procedure

For any chosen generator class, the certificate MUST include a membership check routine:
• parse canonical encoding of G,
• verify generator class ID and parameter tuple correctness,
• verify bounds (channel count, magnitudes, coupling constants),
• verify ordering rules (canonical channel ordering),
• verify any external commitments (EY24Ref hashes, operator encodings),
• return deterministic failure if violated.

3.7 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined admissible generator families AG for EY25: (G1) commutator/unitary
generators, (G2) Lindblad-like generators with controlled dissipation, and (G3) validity-coupled

603



generators referencing EY24. It imposed explicit parameter bounds to prevent tuning smuggling,
defined a conservative baseline profile LIOUV-0, and specified deterministic membership checks.
Chapter 4 next defines discretization and transcript semantics in detail: allowed step types,
deterministic schedules, ordering/rounding rules, transcript commitments, and failure modes for
non-convergence or protocol violation.

4 Discretization, Transcript Semantics, and Deterministic Re-
play

4.1 Purpose

EY25 is not “a differential equation”; it is a contract that deterministically produces an evolution
map and a replayable transcript. This chapter fixes:

• allowed discretization step types and their evaluation order,
• deterministic schedule semantics (time horizon, step count, rounding),
• transcript commitments (what is hashed per step and how),
• and deterministic failure codes for divergence, overflow, or protocol violation.

Rule. Any unspecified solver freedom is forbidden. If a method uses tolerances, iteration caps,
or adaptive steps, those MUST be explicit and deterministic and MUST appear in SpecID.

4.2 Time and Schedule Binding

Schedule Object

EY25 defines a schedule object:

Schedule := (T, ∆t, Nsteps, GridRule),

where T is the total time horizon, ∆t is the step size, and Nsteps is the number of steps.

Rule (two-of-three binding). The SpecID MUST fix any two of (T,∆t,Nsteps), and the
third MUST be derived deterministically. If the derived value is not an integer where required,
the verifier MUST return FAIL_DISC_MISMATCH.

GridRule. GridRule MUST specify:
• rounding policy (floor/ceil/nearest) for derived values,
• whether endpoints are included,
• and whether a final partial step is permitted (default: forbidden).

4.3 Allowed Step Types (Normative Baseline Set)

Let Φ(ρ) ≡ L(ρ) (or Φ(g) ≡ L∗(g) in observable picture). All step types below MUST specify
deterministic evaluation order.

604



D1: Forward Euler (Explicit)

State-side.
ρn+1 := ρn + ∆tΦ(ρn).

Observable-side.
gn+1 := gn + ∆tΦ(gn).

Normative note. Euler is included because it is trivially replayable. Stability is not guaranteed;
failure modes are explicit.

D2: RK2 / Midpoint (Explicit)

State-side.

k1 := Φ(ρn), ρ̃ := ρn + ∆t
2 k1, k2 := Φ(ρ̃), ρn+1 := ρn + ∆t k2.

All intermediate rounding and canonical serialization steps MUST be specified in NumericModel.

D3: Fixed-Rule Trotter Product (For Commutator Generators)

For G1 (commutator) generators, a Trotter step may be defined by a declared factorization:
∑J

H = H(j),
j=1

with a canonical order of terms. A first-order Trotter step is:
∏J

U∆t ≈ exp(−i∆tH(j)),
j=1

and:
ρn+1 := U∆t ρn U

†
∆t.

Rule. If D3 is used, the exponential approximation method MUST be fixed and deterministic
(e.g. fixed-degree Padé with fixed scaling rule and explicit rounding). “Library expm” without a
pinned algorithm is forbidden.

4.4 Rounding and Canonicalization Within a Step

To guarantee replayability, NumericModel MUST define when values are canonicalized.

Canonicalization points. A canonicalization point is a step-local boundary at which the
object is serialized and rounded according to NumericModel. EY25 requires at minimum:

• canonicalize after each step output (ρn+1 or gn+1),
• canonicalize any intermediate object that is included in transcript commitments.

Rule. If two implementations canonicalize at different points, they are different artifacts unless
the SpecID declares CanonPoints explicitly and identically.

605



4.5 Transcript Semantics

TranscriptSpec

EY25 defines:

TranscriptSpec := (CommitType, CommitRule, HashAlg, SerializeRule, CommitRate).

CommitType (examples).
• full-state: commit hash of full canonical encoding of ρn (or gn),
• summary: commit hash of declared summary vector (spectral moments, traces, bucketed

invariants),
• hybrid: periodic full-state commitments plus per-step summaries.

CommitRate. CommitRate MUST be explicit:

CommitRate ∈ {every step, every m steps, schedule list}.

Rule. If summary commitments are used, the summary function MUST be deterministic and
MUST be sufficient to detect protocol deviation as declared by SpecID. Otherwise the artifact
MUST not claim audit-native replay for full trajectories.

Transcript Generation

Let Enc(·) be canonical encoding and Hash(·) be( the decla)red hash. Then:

Txn := Hash Enc(Xn) ,

where Xn is either the full object or the declared summary, per TranscriptSpec.

Rule (chain binding). Optionally, EY25 allows chained commitments:

Txn := Hash(Txn−1 ∥ Enc(Xn)),

but the choice MUST be fixed in TranscriptSpec.

4.6 Deterministic Failure Modes During Evolution

Evolution must fail deterministically when required invariants are violated.

Required failure codes

At minimum, EY25 MUST define:
• FAIL_DISC_MISMATCH: schedule cannot be derived deterministically or violates

GridRule.
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH: truncation calculus is inconsistent across steps or across

required N .

606



• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH: generator action not defined on current object under
Calc/AdjointSpec.

• FAIL_OVERFLOW: numeric overflow/NaN/Inf appears where forbidden by Numeric-
Model.

• FAIL_DIVERGENCE: declared norm proxy exceeds bound Bdiv (if divergence bound
enabled).

• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM: replay produces different intermediate values or tran-
script commitments.

• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH: transcript commitments do not match replay.

Optional divergence bound

EY25 may include an optional bound:

∥Xn∥proxy ≤ Bdiv ∀n,

where ∥·∥proxy is fixed in NumericModel. If enabled and violated, return FAIL_DIVERGENCE.

4.7 Deterministic Replay Definition

Definition 4.1 (Deterministic Replay). An EY25 instance is replay-deterministic if, for any
verifier executing the declared Disc, Trunc, and NumericModel on the same public inputs, the
produced transcript (Txn) and outputs (Xn) match exactly (or within declared tolerance at
declared canonicalization points).

Rule. An EY25 artifact MUST NOT claim replay determinism unless TranscriptSpec and
NumericModel jointly fix all non-deterministic degrees of freedom (ordering, rounding, parallel
reduction, and any randomness).

4.8 Chapter Summary

This chapter fixed discretization semantics for audit-native evolution: schedule binding, allowed
step types with deterministic evaluation order, canonicalization points, transcript commitment
rules, and deterministic failure modes for divergence or protocol violation. It also defined
deterministic replay as the central correctness notion for Laudit.
Chapter 5 next specifies the certificate payload πLIOUV and verifier checks: membership of the
generator, correctness of the discretization protocol, correctness of transcript commitments, and
interoperability checks when composing with EY23/EY24/EY29/EY28.

5 Certificate and Verifier: Replay, Commitments, and Accep-
tance

5.1 Purpose

EY25 publishes evolution as an auditable contract. This chapter specifies:
• the certificate payload πLIOUV required to publish an EY25 instance,

607



• the deterministic verifier checks that accept or reject the instance,
• transcript commitments and replay rules,
• and required failure codes.

EY25 certificates conform to EY22 certificate conventions (EY22 Chapter 5, Appendix A.1) and
add EY25-specific fields and checks.

5.2 Certificate Object πLIOUV

Rule. An EY25 instance MUST be published with a certificate πLIOUV that includes, at
minimum, the following canonical content.

Header (required)

• artifact type: LIOUV

• artifact symbol: Laudit

• SpecID short form and full SpecID tuple
• version identifier

SpecID (required)

The full SpecID tuple MUST be embedded:

(LIOUV, Pic, G, AG, Disc, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Inputs (required)

Inputs MUST include:
• canonical encoding (or commitment) of G and all referenced operators/channels (e.g. H,
{Lk}, EY24Ref),

• AG family definition and membership check ID,
• full Disc and Trunc objects (including schedule constants and truncation levels),
• full NumericModel (rounding, ordering, tolerances, canonicalization points),
• full TranscriptSpec (commit type, hash, serialization, commit rate),
• public initial condition X0 (or its commitment and reconstruction rule),
• any public inputs used to derive schedule or truncation parameters (seed, dataset IDs, basis

IDs), committed by hash if external.

Outputs (required)

Outputs MUST include:
• transcript commitments Tx = (Tx0, . . . ,TxT ) for all required commitment points,
• final output object XT (or its commitment),

608



• any declared summaries (trace, norms, spectral moments) that are committed or used for
checks,

• output hashes for G, Disc, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, and the transcript itself.

Checks (required)

The certificate MUST list check IDs and what each check verifies, grouped as:
• structural and SpecID checks,
• generator membership and feasibility checks,
• discretization protocol checks,
• truncation checks,
• transcript/replay checks,
• interoperability checks (if claimed).

Commitments (required if external objects exist)

All external objects (basis definitions, operator encodings too large to inline, channel catalogs,
transcripts, code snapshots) MUST be committed by hash according to EY22 Appendix A.1.

5.3 Verifier Contract

A verifier takes (πLIOUV) and deterministically returns:

{ACCEPT, REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗}.

Rule. The verifier MUST NOT require trust in producer identity, informal descriptions, or
uncommitted external resources.

5.4 Required Verifier Checks (Normative)

This section enumerates the minimal checks required for EY25 acceptance.

L1: Structural Validity (CCE)

• parse canonical certificate encoding (EY22 CCE rules),
• reject malformed encodings, duplicate keys, non-canonical numbers,
• confirm required fields exist.

Failure: REJECT_MALFORMED.

L2: SpecID Completeness and Consistency

• SpecID tuple is present and complete,
• ArtifactType = LIOUV,

609



• Pic is declared,
• Disc, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec present.

Failure: REJECT_SPECID_MISSING, REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH.

L3: No Hidden Inputs

• G and all referenced operators/channels are provided or committed,
• any derivations (schedule/truncation) depend only on public committed inputs,
• no undeclared randomness is used.

Failure: REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT, FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH.

L4: Generator Membership and Bounds

Verify G ∈ AG deterministically:
• parse canonical encoding of G,
• verify generator class ID (G1/G2/G3),
• verify parameter bounds (channel count, magnitudes, coupling constants on quantized

grids),
• verify canonical ordering rules (e.g. channels lex-sorted by encoding),
• verify any referenced EY24Ref binds to full EY24 SpecID and commitment.

Failure: FAIL_CONSTRAINT.

L5: Discretization Protocol Check

• derive schedule values from SpecID (two-of-three rule),
• verify GridRule and rounding policy,
• verify step type is allowed and all evaluation order is declared,
• verify canonicalization points are declared and consistent with NumericModel.

Failure: FAIL_DISC_MISMATCH or FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

L6: Truncation Protocol Check

• verify Trunc object is complete (Basis, CutRule, BoundaryRule, required Nℓ),
• verify truncation maps for referenced operators (e.g. H 7→ HN ) are deterministic,
• verify CrossNPolicy if multiple truncation levels are used.

Failure: FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

610



L7: Step Execution Replay (Deterministic)

Run the declared protocol from X0 for all required steps:
• execute the step type with deterministic evaluation order,
• apply canonicalization at declared points,
• compute per-step commitments per TranscriptSpec.

Rule. If the verifier cannot execute within declared constraints (e.g. domain mismatch), it
MUST fail deterministically.
Failures:

• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH if generator action not defined,
• FAIL_OVERFLOW if NaN/Inf/overflow occurs where forbidden,
• FAIL_DIVERGENCE if divergence bound is enabled and violated,
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM if replay differs at declared canonicalization points.

L8: Transcript Commitment Check

Compare replayed commitments to the published transcript:

Tx(replay)
n =? Tx(published)

n for all required n.

Failure: FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

L9: Optional Invariant Checks (If Declared)

If SpecID declares invariant checks (trace preservation, positivity preservation, contractive bounds,
etc.), the verifier MUST check them. Failures use: FAIL_INVARIANT or a more specific
code if declared.

L10: Interop Checks (Only if Claimed)

If the certificate claims interoperability with EY23/EY24/EY29/EY28, the verifier MUST
evaluate the declared compatibility predicates under shared NumericModel and declared calculus
(EY22 Chapter 6). Failure: FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE (or the specific EY22 interop
failure code).

5.5 Required Failure Codes

EY25 MUST support at minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH

611



• FAIL_DISC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_OVERFLOW
• FAIL_DIVERGENCE
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH
• FAIL_CONSTRAINT
• FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE
• FAIL_INVARIANT

6 Interop Declarations (Mini): Composition with EY23/EY24/EY29/EY28

6.1 Purpose

This chapter instantiates EY22 interoperability rules (EY22 Chapter 6) for EY25. It defines
minimal compatibility predicates for composing the Audit-Native Liouvillian Laudit with:

• EY23 (CSF) Canonical Spectral Filter F⋆(H),
• EY24 (VPO) Validity Penalty Operator V = C†C,
• EY29 (CGR) Coarse-Grain Reduction R,
• EY28 (INTW) Regime Transport T1→2.

Rule. If an EY25 instance claims interoperability beyond what is stated here, it MUST
introduce additional compatibility predicates inside its Interop SpecID component and MUST
remain checkable under NumericModel.

6.2 Interop Component (EY25)

EY25 declares the following baseline composition forms (EY22 C1–C5):
InteropEY25 := {C4,C1},

i.e. superoperator action (C4) and algebraic composition at the generator/observable level (C1).
Coarse-grain (C3) and transport (C2) are supported only via explicit predicates below.

612



6.3 Compatibility Predicates

All compatibility predicates below are deterministic booleans under the declared NumericModel(s).

LIOUV↔CSF: Filter–Evolve–Filter Workflows

The canonical pattern is:

X −−Fi−lt−er→ X ′ −−L−au−d−it→ X ′′ −−Fi−lt−er→ X⋆,

where filtering may occur on H, on observables, or as a post-processing map on outputs (as
declared by EY23).

Workflow semantics (must be declared). EY25 recognizes two interop semantics with
EY23:

(FE1) generator-side filtering. Filter modifies the generator input (typically H):

H ′ := F⋆(H) or H ′ := Φ(F⋆(H)),

then Laudit is constructed from H ′.

(FE2) output-side filtering. Laudit evolves X and EY23 filtering applies to resulting ob-
jects/summaries.

7 LIOUV-0 Reference Profile and Example SpecID Instance

7.1 Purpose

Chapters 1–6 defined EY25 in full generality. This chapter provides a concrete, audit-friendly
baseline configuration called LIOUV-0. LIOUV-0 is designed to be:

• simple enough to verify by third parties without specialized solvers,
• deterministic by construction (replayable transcript),
• minimal in degrees of freedom (anti-smuggling),
• and stable as a canonical meaning of “audit-native evolution” for Vol. No. IV.

Rule. A LIOUV-0 instance MUST be fully specified by explicit constants (or hash commitments)
and MUST NOT require instance-specific tuning.

7.2 LIOUV-0 Summary (Normative)

LIOUV-0 fixes:
• picture: Pic = state (state-side evolution),
• generator class: G1 commutator generator L(ρ) = −i[H, ρ],
• discretization: D1 Forward Euler with explicit schedule binding,
• transcript: full-state commitment every step (chained commitments allowed but must be

fixed),
• truncation: a fixed basis and cut rule with a fixed truncation schedule {Nℓ},
• certificate: EY22-CCE with required checks L1–L8 (and L10 if interop claimed).

Normative note. LIOUV-0 is intentionally conservative. It defines a clean replay baseline.
Optimized profiles may replace D1 with RK2 or Trotter, or enable controlled dissipation, but
MUST still remain deterministic and transcript-replayable.

7.7 LIOUV-0 NumericModel (Minimal Deterministic Profile)

LIOUV-0 requires a deterministic NumericModel sufficient to fix all replay degrees of freedom:
• arithmetic type (fixed-point or deterministic float) for matrix products,
• rounding policy and precision,
• matrix multiplication order and accumulation order,
• canonicalization points CanonPoints0,
• tolerances εH , εstep (if approximate),
• divergence bound Bdiv (optional; off by default in LIOUV-0).

Recommended (informational). Use exact fixed-point for inputs/parameters (operator
encodings) and deterministic float for step computations with canonical rounding.

LIOUV-0 requires at minimum the checks:
• L1 (CCE structural),
• L2 (SpecID consistency),
• L3 (no hidden inputs),
• L4 (generator membership and bounds),
• L5 (discretization protocol),
• L6 (truncation protocol),
• L7 (step replay),
• L8 (transcript matching).

Interop checks (L10) are required only if interop is claimed.

Next. Chapter 8 fixes the publication boundary and non-claims for EY25 and states licensing
intent, consistent with Vol. No. IV.

8 Publication Boundary, Non-Claims, and Licensing Intent

8.1 Purpose

EY25 makes “dynamics” publishable as an auditable artifact. That power also creates a common
failure mode: people read an evolution protocol as a claim about truth, correctness, or security.
This chapter fixes:

• what MUST be public for an EY25 publication,
• what EY25 explicitly does not claim,
• and the QFC-consistent licensing intent for implementations and derivative catalogs.

8.2 Publication Boundary (Normative)

Rule (what must be public). An EY25 publication MUST include, at minimum:
• the full SpecIDEY25 tuple,
• the canonical encoding (or hash commitment) of the generator G,
• canonical encodings (or commitments) for all referenced operators/channels (e.g. H, {Lk},
C, V , EY24Ref),

• the full Disc object (step type, schedule binding, ordering, canonicalization points),
• the full Trunc object (basis, cut rule, boundary rule, required truncation levels),
• the full NumericModel (rounding, ordering, tolerances, aggregation, canonical encoding

rules),
• the full TranscriptSpec (commit type, serialization, hash algorithm, commit rate, chaining),
• the transcript commitments Tx at all required commitment points,
• and the certificate πLIOUV with required check identifiers.

Rule (no hidden solver degrees of freedom). Any choice that can change the evolution
output MUST be included in SpecID or committed by hash. In particular:

621



• adaptive step size is forbidden unless the schedule is fully specified as a deterministic
function of public inputs,

• any tolerance must be explicit and fixed,
• any randomness must be seeded deterministically and the seed must be public/committed.

Rule (transcript is part of the publication). If an EY25 result is cited as an artifact-derived
claim (trajectory, invariant, regime classification), then the transcript commitments MUST be
published at the declared rate. Claims without transcript commitments MUST be treated as
non-audited narratives.

Rule (commitment for external objects). If the instance references external objects (basis
definitions, generator catalogs, datasets, code snapshots), those objects MUST be committed by
hash according to EY22 Appendix A.1.

8.3 Non-Claims (Explicit)

EY25 explicitly does not claim the following:

NC1: Physical Correctness

EY25 does not claim that the chosen generator G describes physical reality, nor that the resulting
evolution is the “true” time evolution of any system. EY25 only claims:

• the artifact is well-defined under SpecID,
• the verifier checks pass deterministically,
• and replay reproduces the transcript commitments under NumericModel.

NC2: Numerical Optimality

EY25 does not claim that the chosen discretization is numerically optimal, stable, or efficient. A
method can be audit-native and still be a poor integrator. Optimization is outside the baseline
contract (though future profiles may standardize it).

NC3: Security Guarantees Beyond Declared Checks

EY25 does not claim cryptographic security, adversarial robustness, or protection against malicious
producers beyond what is explicitly covered by:

• membership checks for G,
• transcript commitments and deterministic replay,
• and explicit interop predicates.

NC4: Equivalence of Pictures and Semantics

EY25 does not claim that state-side and observable-side evolution are equivalent in all truncation
schemes or numeric models. Pic is part of SpecID, and workflows MUST not conflate them.

622



NC5: Completeness of the Transcript

A transcript commitment proves replay under the declared commitment policy. If TranscriptSpec
commits only to summaries, EY25 does not claim full-state replayability. Any claim about full
trajectories MUST publish full-state commitments at the required rate.

8.4 Responsible Use and Misuse Boundary

Rule. EY25 SHOULD be used to publish evolutions as reproducible artifacts:
• publish SpecID and all committed objects,
• publish transcript commitments,
• and allow third parties to replay and dispute both the generator choice and the discretization

choice.

Misuse examples (non-normative).
• Publishing a trajectory plot without publishing transcript commitments.
• Claiming physical or security guarantees from auditability alone.
• Hiding step-size adaptation or tolerances behind “implementation details”.
• Using non-canonical libraries for matrix exponentials without pinning the algorithm and

rounding rules.

8.5 Licensing Intent (QFC-Consistent)

EY25 is part of the QFC operator suite. The intent is that the specification remains public and
auditable, while enabling controlled licensing of implementations or derivative operator catalogs
if desired.

Normative statement of intent.
• The definitions, SpecID schemas, transcript rules, and verifier requirements are intended to

be publicly readable and reusable.
• Implementations may be licensed under terms chosen by the project (open, dual-license, or

commercial), provided they preserve auditability (SpecID + commitments + transcript +
checks).

• Trademark and naming conventions (QFC, Vol. No. IV, EY-IDs, artifact names) may be
governed separately from the text license.

Rule (no audit stripping). No license arrangement may remove the requirement to publish
SpecID, commitments, and transcript commitments for any claim that relies on EY25.

8.6 Chapter Summary

This chapter fixed the publication boundary for EY25 and listed explicit non-claims: no claims
of physical correctness, numerical optimality, or security beyond declared checks; no implicit
equivalence of pictures; and no full-state replay claim without full-state commitments. It also

623



stated QFC-consistent licensing intent: keep the spec auditable and public while allowing
implementation licensing provided auditability is preserved.

which packages deterministic, replayable discrete-time programs that can generate data for EY23
probing and can be audited under the same transcript conventions.

Chapter 26

EY26: Floquet Program Token UF
Canonical Operator Artifacts for QFC

Enter Yourname

Abstract
This whitepaper defines the Floquet Program Token UF , a canonical
discrete-time execution artifact for QFC workflows. A token packages a
finite, replayable program—an ordered list of operator updates, schedule
semantics, and numeric/truncation rules—into a single auditable object.
Unlike informal “circuits” or opaque simulation scripts, UF is bound by
SpecID: its step list, parameter grids, rounding behavior, tie-breaks, and
failure modes are fixed and verifiable.

UF is designed to generate deterministic datasets for canonical spectral probing (EY23), to interact
with validity penalties (EY24), and to be evolved or audited under audit-native superoperators
(EY25). The token also serves as a portable program commitment: a verifier can check that
execution exactly matches the published transcript commitments, enabling public reproducibility
without trust.

1 Motivation, Scope, and Design Goals

1.1 Motivation: Programs Must Become Publishable Objects

In Vol. No. IV we treat operators as publishable artifacts: they have SpecIDs, deterministic
evaluation rules, and certificates. However, a large class of real workflows is not a single operator
but a finite program: an ordered sequence of operator updates applied over discrete time.
Without a canonical representation, programs drift into:

• informal “circuits” whose semantics depend on libraries,
• scripts with hidden randomness, implicit tolerances, and uncommitted environment details,
• non-deterministic execution due to parallel reduction or GPU scheduling,
• and unverifiable claims about what was actually executed.

EY26 defines the Floquet Program Token UF as a remedy: a program is packaged as a single
auditable object whose meaning is fixed by SpecID and whose execution produces a replayable
transcript.

1.2 What This Whitepaper Defines

EY26 defines:
• the Floquet Program Token UF as a canonical discrete-time execution artifact,



• a program encoding: an ordered step list with explicit update semantics,
• schedule binding (period, step count, time slicing) and deterministic replay rules,
• numeric and truncation semantics required for deterministic execution,
• certificate payload and verifier checks for acceptance,
• minimal interoperability declarations with EY23 (CSF), EY24 (VPO), EY25 (LIOUV),

and optionally EY29/EY28.

1.3 Scope

In-scope.
• Discrete-time programs with a finite step list (or a finite loop with bounded iteration

count).
• Programs that can be executed deterministically under a declared NumericModel and

Truncation policy.
• Transcript commitments that bind the exact executed sequence to public inputs.
• Composition with operator artifacts: filtering, validity, audit evolution, coarse-grain reduc-

tion, and transport.

Out-of-scope.
• Arbitrary Turing-complete programs with unbounded loops or hidden I/O.
• Programs whose semantics depend on non-committed external state (OS time, network

calls, nondeterministic RNG).
• Claims of physical correctness, optimality, or security beyond verifier checks.

1.4 Interpretation: What UF Is

A Floquet Program Token is a portable commitment to a finite execution trace.

Two equivalent views (declared by SpecID). EY26 supports two canonical interpretations:

(P1) Operator product token. UF denotes a finite ordered product:

∏m
UF := Uj ,

j=1

with a declared order convention (left-to-right or right-to-left) fixed by SpecID.

(P2) Step-list execution token. UF denotes a step list executed on an object X:

Xj+1 := Stepj(Xj), j = 0, . . . ,m− 1.

The token commits to the full step list, schedule, and numeric rules.

626



Rule. A token MUST declare whether it is interpreted as (P1), (P2), or both with an explicit
equivalence mapping. If undeclared, the token MUST be rejected as ambiguous.

1.5 Design Goals (Normative)

G1: Deterministic Replay

Executing UF under the declared NumericModel MUST yield the same intermediate states and
transcript commitments across verifiers. No hidden randomness is permitted.

G2: Canonical Program Encoding

The step list MUST be canonically encoded. Reordering steps, changing rounding points, or
changing schedule semantics produces a different token.

G3: Boundedness and Anti-Smuggling

Tokens MUST be finite and bounded:
• bounded step count m ≤ mmax,
• bounded parameter ranges on quantized grids,
• bounded external references, committed by hash if external.

Tokens MUST NOT hide tuning freedom under “implementation details”.

G4: Explicit Failure Codes

When execution fails, it MUST fail deterministically with structured failure codes: domain
mismatch, truncation mismatch, overflow, transcript mismatch, etc.

G5: Composability as a First-Class Contract

Tokens SHOULD compose with:
• EY23 (generate deterministic datasets for probing),
• EY24 (include validity constraints or produce validity-audited outputs),
• EY25 (be embedded inside an audit-native evolution workflow),

under explicit interoperability predicates (EY22 Chapter 6).

G6: Conservative Baseline Profile

EY26 MUST provide a baseline token profile (FLOQ-0) that is trivial to verify: small step lists,
explicit rounding points, and full transcript commitments.

1.6 Chapter Summary

This chapter motivated EY26 as the missing primitive for making programs publishable artifacts.
It fixed the scope (finite discrete-time step lists), defined UF as a portable commitment to execu-

627



tion semantics, and stated design goals: deterministic replay, canonical encoding, boundedness,
explicit failure codes, and composability.
Chapter 2 next defines the normative artifact structure and SpecID binding for UF : step encoding,
schedule semantics, truncation and NumericModel requirements, transcript commitments, and
verifier acceptance.

2 Normative Definition and SpecID Binding

2.1 Conformance to EY22

EY26 inherits Vol. No. IV conventions from EY22:
• SpecID binding (EY22 Chapter 3),
• NumericModel determinism (EY22 Chapter 4),
• certificate schema and verifier checks (EY22 Chapter 5, Appendix A.1),
• interoperability vocabulary (EY22 Chapter 6).

Any deviation MUST be explicitly stated in SpecIDEY26.

2.2 Core Objects

A Floquet Program Token packages a finite program as a canonical object.

Program target. A token acts on a declared target type X:
X ∈ X ,

where X is a declared space (states, observables, operator tuples, summary vectors, or a declared
hybrid object).

Program semantics. EY26 supports:
• Step-list semantics (execution): Xj+1 := Stepj(Xj),
• Operator-product semantics (token operator): UF := ∏m

j=1 Uj ,
with the choice bound by SpecID.

2.3 Artifact Definition

Definition 2.1 (Floquet Program Token). An EY26 artifact instance is a tuple:
UF := (Sem, X , Steps, Sched, Trunc, NumericModel),

together with a certificate πFLOQ that proves:
• the step list Steps is admissible under a declared admissible family ASteps,
• Sched deterministically binds time slicing / period semantics,
• Trunc and NumericModel deterministically bind evaluation and canonicalization,
• and the published transcript commitments match deterministic replay.

628



Rule (finite and bounded). A token MUST be finite. Any loop MUST have a bounded
iteration count fixed in SpecID. Tokens with unbounded control flow are invalid.

2.4 Step Encoding Steps

Step List Structure

Steps := (Step1, . . . ,Stepm), 1 ≤ m ≤ mmax.

Each Stepj MUST be canonically encoded as:

Stepj := (OpTypej , OpRefj , θj , ApplyRulej , CanonPointj).

Fields.
• OpTypej : step type identifier (e.g. unitary update, channel update, projection, filter call,

summary extraction).
• OpRefj : operator reference: either canonical encoding or hash commitment to the operator

object.
• θj : parameter tuple on a declared quantized grid.
• ApplyRulej : how the operator acts on X (left, right, conjugation, superoperator action,

etc.).
• CanonPointj : whether to canonicalize after this step and how.

Rule. Any field that can change execution output MUST be inside the step encoding. Hidden
defaults are forbidden.

Step Types (Baseline Set)

EY26 standardizes a minimal baseline set of step types; future profiles may extend it.

S1: Left action.
X 7→ AX.

S2: Right action.
X 7→ XA.

S3: Conjugation action.
X 7→ AXA†,

with AdjointSpec and rounding points declared in NumericModel.

S4: Superoperator action.
X 7→ S(X),

where S is a declared superoperator (may reference EY25).

629



S5: Projection / penalty step.

X 7→ Proj(X;V ) or X 7→ X − η∇ΦV (X),

where V may reference EY24 and all hyperparameters η are quantized and explicit.

S6: Filter call. Invoke EY23 filter artifact on a declared object:

X 7→ Filter(X;F⋆).

If used, it MUST bind to EY23 SpecID.

Rule. If a step type references another artifact (EY23/EY24/EY25), the token MUST include
interop predicates and references to those artifacts’ SpecIDs (or commitments).

2.5 Schedule Semantics Sched

Sched binds Floquet/period semantics and time slicing.

Sched Component (required)

Sched := (PeriodType, T, ∆t, m, OrderConv, RepeatCount, StopRule).

PeriodType.
• finite: execute exactly m steps once,
• floquet: interpret the step list as one period and repeat R times (bounded),
• schedule-list: execute steps according to an explicit index list (bounded).

Rule (bounded repeats). If repeats are allowed, RepeatCount = R MUST be fixed and
bounded: R ≤ Rmax.

OrderConv. Order convention MUST be explicit:

OrderConv ∈ {left-to-right, right-to-left}.

This matters for operator-product semantics and for step-list semantics if intermediate canonical-
ization points are present.

2.6 Truncation Semantics Trunc

Tokens may depend on truncation calculus (finite representations of operators and objects).

Trunc Component (required if infinite objects exist).

Trunc := (Basis, CutRule, BoundaryRule, {Nℓ}, CrossNPolicy).

This reuses EY22 truncation vocabulary.

630



Rule. If truncation is used, the required truncation levels {Nℓ} MUST be fixed in SpecID and
applied consistently to all steps that require finite representation.

2.7 Transcript Contract

A token MUST publish transcript commitments that bind execution.

TranscriptSpec

TranscriptSpec := (CommitType, HashAlg, SerializeRule, CommitRate, ChainRule).

CommitType.
• full-X: hash full canonical encoding of Xj at commitment points,
• summary: hash a declared summary vector extracted from Xj ,
• hybrid: periodic full-X plus per-step summary.

Rule. If a token claims full replay of intermediate states, it MUST commit full-X at the required
rate. Summary-only commitments cannot claim full-state replay determinism.

2.8 SpecID for EY26

ArtifactType. For EY26:
ArtifactType = FLOQ.

SpecID components (EY26 binding). The full SpecID tuple is:

SpecIDEY26 := (FLOQ, Sem, X , Steps, ASteps, Sched, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Sem (required)

Sem ∈ {step-list, operator-product, both}
MUST be declared.

X (required)

X MUST declare the target object type and its canonical encoding rule.

Steps and ASteps (required)

Even if the step list is provided, ASteps MUST exist to enforce bounds, canonical ordering, and
parameter grids.

Sched, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec (required)

These bind deterministic execution and transcript commitments.

631



Cert, Interop, Version (required)

Cert binds verifier checks; Interop binds compatibility predicates; Version binds meaning and
MUST change if any component changes.

2.9 Deterministic Outcomes

EY26 verification MUST return:

{ACCEPT,REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗},

and MUST support at minimum:
• FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH
• FAIL_STEP_MALFORMED
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_OVERFLOW
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_CONSTRAINT

2.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined EY26 as a canonical token artifact that packages a finite program: a step
list with explicit apply rules, a schedule binding for Floquet semantics, truncation and numeric
rules for deterministic evaluation, and a transcript contract for verifiable replay. It fixed the
SpecID binding and minimal failure codes.
Chapter 3 next defines admissible step families ASteps: step bounds, parameter grids, canonical
ordering, allowed step-type catalogs, and anti-smuggling constraints for program tokens.

3 Admissible Step Families ASteps: Canonical Program Classes

3.1 Purpose of ASteps

A token is meaningful only if its step list is meaningfully constrained. Otherwise, “a token” can
smuggle arbitrary behavior: hidden tuning via continuous parameters, non-canonical operator
encodings, or external dependencies that cannot be replayed.
Therefore, ASteps is normative. It specifies:

• which step types are allowed,
• how each step is parameterized and bounded,
• which operator references are permitted and how they are committed,
• and how the full program is canonically ordered and verified.

632



Rule. A step list Steps is admissible only if:
• each step belongs to an allowed step-type catalog,
• all parameters lie on declared quantized grids with explicit bounds,
• all operator references are canonical or hash-committed,
• the overall program satisfies global boundedness (step count, repeat count, memory bounds),
• and membership is checkable deterministically under NumericModel.

3.2 Canonical Encoding and Anti-Ambiguity

Rule (canonical step serialization). Every step Stepj MUST have a canonical encoding
Enc(Stepj) and MUST be serializable in a fixed field order:

(OpType, OpRef, θ, ApplyRule, CanonPoint).

No optional fields may be omitted silently; if a field is not used it MUST be explicitly null.

Rule (program encoding). The token encoding is:

Enc(UF ) := Enc(Sem)∥Enc(X )∥Enc(Sched)∥Enc(Trunc)∥Enc(NumericModel)∥Enc(Steps),

with Steps encoded as a length-prefixed list of step encodings.

Rule (no hidden defaults). Any behavior that can affect outputs (rounding points, boundary
conventions, order conventions, stopping rules) MUST be explicitly encoded. If it is not encoded,
it does not exist.

3.3 Step-Type Catalog (Baseline)

EY26 defines a baseline catalog Cstep. Tokens may extend it only by declaring a new catalog ID
and publishing its formal semantics and verifier rules.

Baseline catalog.
C(0)

step := {S1,S2,S3, S4, S5,S6},
where S1–S6 are the baseline step types from Chapter 2.

Rule. A FLOQ-0 token (baseline profile) MUST use only C(0)
step.

3.4 Parameter Grids and Bounds

To prevent tuning smuggling, all parameters MUST be quantized.

Per-step parameter grid

Each step type OpType has an associated parameter grid:

θj ∈ GOpType .j

633



Grid structure (normative). A grid MUST be defined by:

G := (Type, Step, Bound, EncodingRule),

where:
• Type ∈ {fixed-point, integer, enum},
• Step is the quantization step size (if numeric),
• Bound is an explicit max magnitude (or min/max range),
• EncodingRule defines canonical bytes.

Rule. Continuous parameters are forbidden unless they are discretized by a declared grid.

Global bounds

In addition to per-step bounds, a token MUST satisfy:

m ≤ mmax, R ≤ Rmax,

and may include resource bounds (informational unless declared):

WorkProxy(UF ) ≤ Bwork, MemProxy(UF ) ≤ Bmem.

3.5 Operator Reference Policy

Each step may reference an operator or superoperator object.

OpRef modes. OpRef MUST be one of:
• inline: canonical encoding of the operator at required truncation levels,
• commit: a hash commitment, plus a deterministic reconstruction/truncation rule,
• artifact-ref : a reference to another Vol. No. IV artifact SpecID (e.g. EY23/EY24/EY25),

plus its commitment hash.

Rule. If OpRef is commit or artifact-ref, the commitment MUST be included in the certificate
and MUST match replay.

Rule (no external state). OpRefs MUST NOT depend on non-committed external state. If
an operator is loaded from a file, the file hash must be committed.

3.6 Canonical Ordering and Normal Form

Even though execution order matters, there are token-level canonicalization requirements.

634



Program normal form

A step list is in normal form if:
• step indices are consecutive 1, . . . ,m,
• all CanonPointj are explicitly declared,
• all ApplyRulej are explicit and match Sem conventions,
• all parameters θj are in canonical encoding,
• and all OpRefs satisfy the reference policy.

Rule. Tokens not in normal form MUST be rejected (FAIL_STEP_MALFORMED).

Optional canonical step reordering (disabled by default)

EY26 allows the possibility of a canonical reordering rule only if the token declares an equivalence
class (e.g. commuting steps). This is disabled by default.

Rule (default). Unless a token explicitly declares a step-commutation equivalence and a
deterministic reordering rule, no reordering is permitted. The listed order is the executed order.

3.7 Membership Check Procedure

A verifier checks Steps ∈ ASteps deterministically:
• parse token encoding and step list,
• check m ≤ mmax and bounded repeats,
• for each step: check OpType is allowed, OpRef is valid, parameters lie on grids, ApplyRule

and CanonPoint are valid,
• check all commitments resolve deterministically,
• check program is in normal form,
• return deterministic failure codes if violated.

3.8 Baseline Profile FLOQ-0 (Admissibility Defaults)

EY26 defines a conservative baseline admissibility profile.

FLOQ-0 admissibility. A FLOQ-0 token MUST satisfy:

• allowed step catalog: C(0)
step only,

• mmax fixed and small (e.g. mmax = 256),
• repeat count disabled by default (R = 1) unless explicitly enabled,
• parameters on fixed-point grids with explicit bounds,
• OpRefs either inline or hash-committed (artifact-ref allowed only if full SpecIDs are

provided),

635



• full-X transcript commitments at every step (unless declared otherwise).

3.9 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined ASteps for EY26: a normative admissibility framework for program tokens.
It fixed canonical step encoding, baseline step-type catalog, quantized parameter grids and global
bounds, operator reference policy, program normal form, and deterministic membership checks.
It also defined FLOQ-0 admissibility defaults.
Chapter 4 next specifies schedule and execution semantics in detail: Floquet period interpretation,
repeat rules, canonicalization points during execution, transcript generation, and deterministic
failure modes for token execution.

4 Schedule, Execution Semantics, and Deterministic Replay

4.1 Purpose

A token is not only a list of steps. It also fixes how steps are executed: time slicing, repetition
semantics, ordering conventions, canonicalization points, and transcript commitments. This
chapter defines:

• schedule semantics (finite vs Floquet period vs schedule-list),
• execution semantics for step-list and operator-product interpretations,
• canonicalization points and rounding boundaries during execution,
• transcript generation rules,
• and deterministic failure codes for token execution.

Rule. If the same token encoding can produce different outputs on different runtimes, it is not
an EY26 token. Execution MUST be replayable.

4.2 Schedule Semantics Sched
Recall:

Sched := (PeriodType, T, ∆t, m, OrderConv, RepeatCount, StopRule).

PeriodType: finite

Meaning. Execute the step list exactly once:
j = 1, . . . ,m.

RepeatCount MUST equal 1. If RepeatCount ≠ 1, reject with FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH.

PeriodType: floquet

Meaning. Interpret the step list as one period and repeat it R times:
(j, r) ∈ {1, . . . ,m} × {1, . . . , R},

with R = RepeatCount fixed and bounded.

636



Rule (bounded). R MUST be fixed in SpecID and satisfy R ≤ Rmax. Otherwise fail
FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH.

PeriodType: schedule-list

Meaning. Execute steps according to an explicit index list:

I = (i1, . . . , iL), iℓ ∈ {1, . . . ,m},

where I is fixed and canonically encoded in SpecID.

Rule. The index list MUST be bounded (L ≤ Lmax) and canonical. Out-of-range indices cause
FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH.

4.3 Time Binding (Two-of-Three Rule)

Because Floquet language suggests time, EY26 standardizes time binding even for discrete
programs.

Rule (two-of-three binding). The SpecID MUST fix any two of:

(T, ∆t, Nticks),

and deterministically derive the third. Here Nticks is the number of executed step applications:
m, PeriodType = finite

Nticks := mR, PeriodType = floquet
L, PeriodType = schedule-list

If derivation is not consistent, fail FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH.

Note. EY26 does not require that each program step corresponds to physical time; time is a
semantic coordinate for audit and interop.

4.4 Execution Semantics

Let X0 be the public initial object in the declared space X .

Step-List Semantics (Primary)

If Sem = step-list or both, execution is:

Tick order. Define a tick order τ = 1, . . . , Nticks and map each tick to a step index j(τ) by:

τ, finite
j(τ) := 1 + ((τ − 1) mod m), floquet

iτ , schedule-list

Then:
Xτ := Apply(Stepj(τ), Xτ−1).

637



OrderConv. OrderConv MUST still be declared, because it fixes how products are interpreted
if the token also claims operator-product semantics, and it fixes the interpretation of composite
ApplyRules that involve multiple operator multiplications.

Operator-Product Semantics (Secondary)

If Sem = operator-product or both, the token defines:

∏m
UF := Uj

j=1

under the declared OrderConv. If PeriodType = floquet, then the total token is:

Utot := (UF )R.

Rule. If Sem = both, the token MUST declare whether:
• (E1) product semantics are only an annotation, or
• (E2) product semantics are asserted equivalent to step-list execution under declared canoni-

calization points.
If equivalence is asserted, the verifier MUST check it at the declared commitment points, otherwise
FAIL_CONSTRAINT.

4.5 ApplyRule Semantics

Each step includes an ApplyRule. EY26 standardizes a minimal set.

Baseline ApplyRule forms

• AR1 left: X 7→ AX

• AR2 right: X 7→ XA

• AR3 conj: X 7→ AXA†

• AR4 super: X 7→ S(X)
• AR5 update: X 7→ Update(X; θ) with explicit formula

Rule. If ApplyRule refers to an algorithmic update (AR5), the algorithm MUST be fully
specified and deterministic under NumericModel (no adaptive stopping unless explicitly bound).

4.6 Canonicalization Points During Execution

NumericModel MUST declare canonicalization points for token execution.

CanonPoint per step. Each Stepj includes CanonPointj ∈ {none, after, after + summary}
(or an explicitly defined enum).

638



Rule (minimum canonicalization). A FLOQ-0 token MUST canonicalize after every tick:

Xτ −−
C−a−no−n→ X̂τ

and use X̂τ for transcript commitments.

Rule (deterministic rounding). Canonicalization MUST specify:
• rounding mode,
• precision or fixed-point grid,
• ordering for reductions and serialization.

4.7 Transcript Generation

Recall:

TranscriptSpec := (CommitType, HashAlg, SerializeRule, CommitRate, ChainRule).

Commitment points

CommitRate defines a set of commitment ticks Tcommit ⊆ {0, . . . , Nticks}.

Rule. Tcommit MUST be derivable deterministically from SpecID and public inputs. If not, fail
FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH.

Commitment computation

Let Yτ be the committed object at tick τ (full-X (or summ)ary). Then:

Txτ := Hash Enc(Yτ )

or, if chained: ( )
Txτ := Hash Txτ− ∥ Enc(Yτ ) ,

where τ− is the previous commitment tick.

Rule. If summary commitments are used, the summary function MUST be deterministic and
MUST be included in SpecID (or referenced by artifact-ref).

4.8 Deterministic Failure Modes

Token execution MUST fail deterministically when requirements are violated.

Required failure codes

At minimum:
• FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH: schedule derivation fails, invalid indices, repeats out of

bounds.

639



• FAIL_STEP_MALFORMED: invalid step encoding, missing fields, non-canonical
params.

• FAIL_CONSTRAINT: admissibility constraints violated (grid/bounds, equivalence
assertions fail).

• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH: ApplyRule not defined for the declared X under
Calc/AdjointSpec.

• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH: truncation calculus inconsistent across steps or required
N .

• FAIL_OVERFLOW: NaN/Inf/overflow occurs where forbidden.
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM: replay differs at declared canonicalization points.
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH: transcript commitments do not match replay.

4.9 Deterministic Replay Definition

Definition 4.1 (Token Replay Determinism). An EY26 token is replay-deterministic if, for
any verifier executing the declared schedule, step list, truncation, and NumericModel on the
same public inputs, the produced commitment sequence Tx and the committed objects Yτ match
exactly (or within declared tolerance at declared canonicalization points).

Rule. If a token claims full-state replay, it MUST commit full-X at the declared commitment
rate. Summary-only commitments can claim only summary replay.

4.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter fixed schedule semantics (finite/Floquet/schedule-list), execution semantics for
step-list and operator-product interpretations, canonicalization points and rounding boundaries,
transcript generation rules, and deterministic failure modes. It defined replay determinism as
the central correctness notion for program tokens.

5 Certificate and Verifier: Execution Replay and Acceptance

5.1 Purpose

EY26 publishes programs as auditable objects. This chapter specifies:
• the certificate payload πFLOQ required to publish a Floquet Program Token,
• deterministic verifier checks for admissibility, replay, and transcript commitment matching,
• and required failure codes.

Certificates follow EY22 canonical certificate encoding (CCE) conventions (EY22 Chapter 5,
Appendix A.1) and add token-specific fields.

640



5.2 Certificate Object πFLOQ

Rule. An EY26 token MUST be published with a certificate πFLOQ that includes, at minimum,
the following canonical content.

Header (required)

• artifact type: FLOQ

• artifact symbol: UF
• SpecID short form and full SpecID tuple
• version identifier

SpecID (required)

The full SpecID tuple MUST be embedded:

(FLOQ, Sem, X , Steps, ASteps, Sched, Trunc, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Inputs (required)

Inputs MUST include:
• canonical encoding (or hash commitment) of the full step list Steps,
• canonical encoding of ASteps (or its ID + committed definition),
• full Sched object and all public inputs used to derive schedule values,
• full Trunc object (if used) and required truncation levels {Nℓ},
• full NumericModel (rounding, ordering, canonicalization points, tolerances),
• full TranscriptSpec (commit type, hash algorithm, serialization, commit rate, chain rule),
• initial object X0 (or its commitment + deterministic reconstruction rule),
• all external OpRefs (operators, catalogs, datasets) committed by hash according to EY22

Appendix A.1,
• any artifact-refs used by steps (EY23/EY24/EY25 etc.) as SpecIDs + commitment hashes.

Outputs (required)

Outputs MUST include:
• transcript commitments Tx at all required commitment ticks,
• final committed object YNticks (full-X or summary as declared),
• any declared summary vectors used by commitments or checks,
• hash commitments to the final token encoding and to the transcript sequence itself.

641



Checks (required)

The certificate MUST list check IDs and what each check verifies, grouped as:
• structural and SpecID checks,
• step admissibility checks,
• schedule derivation checks,
• truncation checks (if used),
• replay execution checks,
• transcript commitment checks,
• interoperability checks (if claimed).

5.3 Verifier Contract

A verifier takes πFLOQ and deterministically returns:

{ACCEPT, REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗}.

Rule. The verifier MUST NOT depend on producer identity, informal descriptions, or uncom-
mitted runtime details.

5.4 Required Verifier Checks (Normative)

This section enumerates minimal checks required for EY26 acceptance.

F1: Structural Validity (CCE)

• parse canonical certificate encoding (EY22 CCE rules),
• reject malformed encodings, duplicate keys, non-canonical numbers,
• confirm required fields exist.

Failure: REJECT_MALFORMED.

F2: SpecID Completeness and Consistency

• SpecID tuple is present and complete,
• ArtifactType = FLOQ,
• Sem, X , Steps, Sched are present,
• NumericModel and TranscriptSpec are present,
• Trunc is present iff required by target space or OpRefs.

Failure: REJECT_SPECID_MISSING, REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH.

642



F3: No Hidden Inputs

• all OpRefs resolve to canonical encodings or committed objects,
• schedule derivations depend only on public committed inputs,
• no undeclared randomness, I/O, or external state exists.

Failure: REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT, FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH.

F4: Step Admissibility (Membership in ASteps)

Verify Steps ∈ ASteps deterministically:
• parse canonical step encodings; all required fields present,
• verify m ≤ mmax,
• verify each OpType belongs to the allowed catalog ID,
• verify θj lies on declared grids and satisfies bounds,
• verify ApplyRule is valid for declared X and Calc/AdjointSpec,
• verify CanonPoint fields are valid and explicit,
• verify any artifact-refs provide full SpecIDs + commitments,
• verify program normal form (Chapter 3).

Failure: FAIL_STEP_MALFORMED or FAIL_CONSTRAINT.

F5: Schedule Derivation and Consistency

• derive Nticks from PeriodType and bounds (finite/floquet/schedule-list),
• verify RepeatCount R ≤ Rmax if applicable,
• verify time binding (two-of-three rule) where used,
• verify index list bounds and in-range indices for schedule-list.

Failure: FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH.

F6: Truncation Protocol Check (If Used)

• verify Trunc object is complete (Basis, CutRule, BoundaryRule, required Nℓ),
• verify truncation maps for all OpRefs are deterministic,
• verify CrossNPolicy if multiple truncation levels appear.

Failure: FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

F7: Replay Execution (Deterministic)

Run the declared token execution from X0 for all ticks:
• apply steps using the declared tick mapping j(τ),

643



• enforce OrderConv and ApplyRules,
• apply canonicalization at declared CanonPoints,
• compute commitments at commitment ticks.

Failures:
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH if a step action is not defined,
• FAIL_OVERFLOW if NaN/Inf/overflow occurs where forbidden,
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM if replay differs at canonicalization points.

F8: Transcript Commitment Check

Compare replayed commitments to published commitments:

Tx(replay)
τ =? Tx(published)

τ for all τ ∈ Tcommit.

Failure: FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

F9: Optional Equivalence Check (If Sem = both)

If the token asserts equivalence between step-list execution and operator-product semantics, the
verifier MUST check equivalence at declared commitment points:

X̂(step)
τ =? X̂(prod)

τ for all required τ.

Failure: FAIL_CONSTRAINT.

F10: Interop Checks (Only if Claimed)

If interop is claimed with EY23/EY24/EY25/EY29/EY28, the verifier MUST evaluate the
declared compatibility predicates under shared NumericModel and declared calculus (EY22
Chapter 6). Failure: FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE (or the specific EY22 interop failure
code).

5.5 Required Failure Codes

EY26 MUST support at minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_SCHED_MISMATCH
• FAIL_STEP_MALFORMED
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH

644



• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH

• FAIL_OVERFLOW

• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM

• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH

• FAIL_CONSTRAINT

• FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE

6 Interop Declarations (Mini): Composition with EY23/EY24/EY25/EY29/EY28

6.1 Purpose

This chapter instantiates EY22 interoperability rules (EY22 Chapter 6) for EY26. It defines
minimal compatibility predicates for composing the Floquet Program Token UF with:

• EY23 (CSF) Canonical Spectral Filter F⋆(H),
• EY24 (VPO) Validity Penalty Operator V = C†C,
• EY25 (LIOUV) Audit-Native Liouvillian Laudit,
• EY29 (CGR) Coarse-Grain Reduction R,
• EY28 (INTW) Regime Transport T1→2.

Rule. If an EY26 token claims interoperability beyond what is stated here, it MUST introduce
additional compatibility predicates inside its Interop SpecID component and MUST remain
checkable under the declared NumericModel.

6.2 Interop Component (EY26)

EY26 declares the following baseline composition forms (EY22 C1–C5):

InteropEY26 := {C5,C4,C1},

i.e. token execution (C5), superoperator embedding (C4), and algebraic operator composition
(C1). Coarse-grain (C3) and transport (C2) are supported only via explicit predicates below.

645



6.3 Compatibility Predicates

Unless explicitly stated, compatibility is asymmetric (EY22).

A common workflow is:

7 FLOQ-0 Reference Profile and Example SpecID Instance

7.1 Purpose

Chapters 1–6 defined EY26 in full generality. This chapter provides a concrete, audit-friendly
baseline configuration called FLOQ-0. FLOQ-0 is designed to be:

• simple enough to verify by third parties without specialized tooling,
• deterministic by construction (replayable transcript),
• conservative in degrees of freedom (anti-smuggling),
• and a stable reference meaning of “program token” for Vol. No. IV.

Rule. A FLOQ-0 token MUST be fully specified by explicit constants (or hash commitments)
and MUST NOT require instance-specific tuning.

649



7.2 FLOQ-0 Summary (Normative)

FLOQ-0 fixes:
• semantics: Sem = step-list (operator-product semantics optional but not asserted equiva-

lent),
• schedule: PeriodType = finite (no repeats),
• step catalog: baseline C(0)

step only,
• bounded length: m ≤ mmax,0 with a small fixed bound,
• canonicalization: after every tick (and at any commitment point),
• transcript: full-X commitment every tick, optionally hash-chained,
• truncation: fixed basis and cut rule if required by OpRefs,
• certificate: EY22-CCE with required checks F1–F8 (and F10 only if interop is claimed).

Normative note. FLOQ-0 is intentionally conservative. It makes “a program” maximally
verifiable: everything is explicit, bounded, and committed.

Fixed constants (FLOQ-0). FLOQ-0 fixes:

with δ0 and K0 fixed in SpecID.

Rule. If any parameter is not on the declared grid, reject with FAIL_CONSTRAINT.

Trunc0 := (Basis0, CutRule0, BoundaryRule0, N0, CrossNPolicy = none).

Rule. FLOQ-0 uses a single truncation level N0 unless the token explicitly declares a finite list.
Multiple truncation levels introduce complexity and are reserved for non-baseline profiles.

7.6 FLOQ-0 NumericModel and Canonicalization

FLOQ-0 requires a minimal deterministic NumericModel:
• arithmetic type: deterministic fixed-point or deterministic float with explicit rounding,
• rounding mode and precision,
• matrix multiplication order and accumulation order,
• canonicalization after each tick,
• tolerances (default exact for fixed-point; otherwise explicit εstep).

CanonPoints. FLOQ-0 canonicalizes:

Xτ −−
C−a−no−n→ X̂τ for all τ = 0, . . . ,m,

and transcript commitments bind X̂τ .

7.7 FLOQ-0 Transcript Profile

TranscriptSpec0

TranscriptSpec0 := (CommitType = full-X, HashAlg0, SerializeRule = EY22-CCE, CommitRate = every tick, ChainRule0).

ChainRule. FLOQ-0 permits:
• ChainRule0 = none, or
• ChainRule0 = hash-chain.

The choice MUST be fixed in SpecID.

651



7.8 FLOQ-0 Certificate Requirements

FLOQ-0 requires at minimum the checks:
• F1 (CCE structural),
• F2 (SpecID consistency),
• F3 (no hidden inputs),
• F4 (step admissibility),
• F5 (schedule derivation),
• F6 (truncation protocol, if used),
• F7 (replay execution),
• F8 (transcript matching).

Interop checks (F10) are required only if interop is claimed.

This chapter defined FLOQ-0, a conservative baseline profile for EY26 designed for determin-

admissible step catalog and parameter grids, canonicalization after every tick, full transcript
