653



8 Publication Boundary, Non-Claims, and Licensing Intent

8.1 Purpose

EY26 makes programs publishable. That also creates a predictable risk: readers treat an executed
token as a claim about truth, security, or physical correctness. This chapter fixes:

• what MUST be public for an EY26 publication,
• what EY26 explicitly does not claim,
• and QFC-consistent licensing intent for implementations and token catalogs.

8.2 Publication Boundary (Normative)

Rule (what must be public). An EY26 publication MUST include, at minimum:
• the full SpecIDEY26 tuple,
• the full step list Steps in canonical encoding or a hash commitment plus deterministic

reconstruction rule,
• the admissible family ASteps definition (or catalog ID + committed definition),
• the full schedule object Sched including all bound constants and derivation rules,
• the full Trunc object Trunc if truncation is used,
• the full NumericModel (rounding, ordering, canonicalization points, tolerances),
• the full TranscriptSpec (commit type, serialization, hash algorithm, commit rate, chaining),
• transcript commitments Tx at all required commitment ticks,
• the certificate πFLOQ listing required verifier checks (F1–F8 at minimum),
• and hash commitments for all external OpRefs (operators, catalogs, datasets, code snap-

shots) used by steps.

Rule (no hidden environment dependencies). A token MUST NOT depend on:
• OS time, network calls, non-committed files, device identity,
• nondeterministic RNG,
• unspecified GPU parallelism or unspecified reduction order.

If any such dependency exists, the artifact is invalid.

Rule (boundedness is part of publication). Bounds are not optional. The publication
MUST include:

mmax, Rmax, parameter grids and bounds, and any declared work/memory proxies.

Rule (transcript is part of the claim). If any claim relies on the execution of UF , the
transcript commitments MUST be published at the declared rate. Claims without transcript
commitments MUST be treated as non-audited narratives.

654



8.3 Non-Claims (Explicit)

EY26 explicitly does not claim the following:

NC1: Physical Correctness

EY26 does not claim that the token describes physical time evolution or that its steps correspond
to real-world processes. It claims only that the execution is well-defined, bounded, and replayable
under SpecID.

NC2: Computational Optimality

EY26 does not claim that a token is efficient, minimal, optimal, or stable under perturbations.
A token can be perfectly auditable and still be a poor program.

NC3: Security Beyond Declared Checks

EY26 does not claim cryptographic security, robustness to adversarial producers, or resistance to
side-channels beyond what is enforced by:

• admissibility constraints ASteps,
• transcript commitments and replay determinism,
• explicit interop predicates (if claimed).

NC4: Equivalence of Interpretations

If Sem includes operator-product semantics, EY26 does not automatically claim equivalence to
step-list semantics. Equivalence must be explicitly asserted and verified, otherwise operator-
product is at most an annotation.

NC5: Completeness of Commitments

Summary-only transcript commitments do not imply full-state replayability. If a publication
commits only to summaries, it cannot claim full trajectory reproducibility.

8.4 Responsible Use and Misuse Boundary

Recommended use (informational). Use EY26 to publish discrete-time programs where:
• the step list is explicit and bounded,
• parameters are quantized and committed,
• canonicalization points are explicit,
• transcript commitments allow third parties to replay exactly.

Misuse examples (non-normative).
• Publishing a token execution plot without publishing the token encoding and transcript

commitments.

655



• Using “library defaults” for floating point rounding or matrix multiplication order without
pinning NumericModel.

• Smuggling adaptivity (variable step counts, hidden early stopping) behind implementation
freedom.

• Claiming security, privacy, or physical truth from auditability alone.

8.5 Licensing Intent (QFC-Consistent)

EY26 is part of the QFC operator suite. The intent is:
• keep the specification (definitions, SpecID schema, verifier checks) publicly readable and

reusable,
• allow implementations and token catalogs to be licensed under project-chosen terms (open,

dual, or commercial),
• preserve auditability as non-negotiable: SpecID + commitments + transcript + verifier

rules remain required for any claim.

Rule (no audit stripping). No license arrangement may remove the requirement to publish
SpecID, commitments, and transcript commitments for any claim that depends on EY26.

8.6 Chapter Summary

This chapter fixed the publication boundary for EY26 and stated explicit non-claims: no physical
correctness, no computational optimality, no security guarantees beyond declared checks, no
implicit equivalence of semantics, and no full-state reproducibility without full-state commitments.
It also stated QFC-consistent licensing intent: keep the spec auditable and public while allowing
implementation/catalog licensing provided auditability is preserved.

Next. With EY26 complete, Vol. No. IV proceeds to EY27 (Commutant Generator Gcomm),
which standardizes symmetry and commutation constraints as canonical artifacts that restrict
operator families, tokens, and audit-native evolutions.

656



Chapter 27

EY27: Commutant Generator Gcomm
Canonical Operator Artifacts for QFC

Enter Yourname

Abstract
This whitepaper defines the Commutant Generator Gcomm, a canonical
artifact that encodes symmetry and compatibility constraints as a gener-
ator of commutation requirements. Given a target operator or workflow
component, Gcomm produces a testable predicate—and when needed, a
constructive constraint operator—that forces membership in a declared
commutant class.

The intent is to make “symmetry”, “invariants”, and “allowed transformations” auditable:
instead of informal statements (“these operators should commute”), EY27 provides SpecID-bound
commutation rules, numeric and truncation semantics, and certificates enabling deterministic
verification. Gcomm is designed to compose with canonical spectral filtering (EY23), validity
penalties (EY24), audit-native evolution (EY25), program tokens (EY26), regime transport
(EY28), and coarse-grain reduction (EY29).

1 Normative Commutation Modes and Commutator Measures

1.1 Purpose

To make “commutes” machine-checkable, EY27 fixes a minimal vocabulary:
• commutation modes (what equality means and where it is required),
• commutator measures (how violation is quantified),
• tolerance semantics under NumericModel,
• and canonical predicate identifiers that other artifacts can cite in Interop.

Rule. Every EY27 instance MUST declare a commutation mode Mode, a measure Meas, and
a tolerance model. Undeclared commutation semantics are invalid.

1.2 Objects and Domains

Let A,B be operators (or derived objects that admit operator evaluation) acting on a declared
space H, with truncation policy Trunc (if applicable).

Commutator and anticommutator.

[A,B] := AB −BA, {A,B} := AB +BA.



Rule (domain compatibility). All products appearing in the declared commutation relation
MUST be well-defined under declared truncation and calculus. If not, the check MUST fail
deterministically with FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH or FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

1.3 Commutation Modes Mode

EY27 standardizes the following commutation modes.

M1: Exact Commutation (Finite Representation)

Meaning. In the declared finite representation (e.g. truncation level N):

[A,B] = 0 exactly in the declared arithmetic model.

When used. Preferred when NumericModel is exact (fixed-point / rational) and truncation is
explicit.

Predicate form. ( )
CommM1(A,B) := [A,B] = 0 .

M2: Approximate Commutation (Norm-Toleranced)

Meaning.
∥[A,B]∥Meas ≤ ε,

where ε is fixed in SpecID (or quantized on a declared grid).

Rule (tolerance binding). ε MUST be part of SpecID. “Within numerical error” is forbidden
unless ε is explicit.

Predicate form. ( )
CommM2(A,B; ε,Meas) := ∥[A,B]∥Meas ≤ ε .

M3: Projected Commutation (Subspace/Projector)

Meaning. Commutation is required only on a declared subspace, represented by a projector P
(or idempotent):

P [A,B]P = 0 (exact or toleranced).

Variants.
• M3a exact: P [A,B]P = 0.
• M3b approx: ∥P [A,B]P∥Meas ≤ ε.

Rule (projector binding). P MUST be canonically encoded or committed by hash and
MUST satisfy idempotence (exact or within declared tolerance).

658



Predicate form. ( )
CommM3(A,B;P, ε) := ∥P [A,B]P∥Meas ≤ ε ,

with ε = 0 for exact.

M4: Graded Commutation (Commutator vs Anticommutator)

Meaning. Declare whether the relation i{s a commutator or anticommutator constraint:

[A,B]σ := AB −BA, σ = −
AB +BA, σ = +

and require [A,B]σ = 0 (exact or approx).

Predicate form. ( )
CommM4(A,B;σ, ε) := ∥[A,B]σ∥Meas ≤ ε .

M5: Central-Phase Commutation (Projective)

Meaning. Some workflows require commutation up to a central phase (typical for unitary
tokens):

AB ≈ eiϕBA,
with ϕ on a declared grid.

Predicate form. ( )
CommM5(A,B;ϕ, ε) := ∥AB − eiϕBA∥Meas ≤ ε .

Rule (phase binding). ϕ MUST be quantized and bounded, and the grid MUST be declared
in SpecID.

1.4 Commutator Measures Meas
A commutation mode needs a measure for “how much” it fails.

Rule. Every EY27 instance MUST declare one commutator measure identifier Meas and its
computation semantics under NumericModel.

N1: Frobenius Norm √
∥X∥F := Tr(X†X).

Deterministic under canonical multiplication and trace ordering.

N2: Operator Norm Proxy

Exact operator norm is expensive; EY27 standardizes a proxy:
∥X∥op_proxy := max ∥Xvk∥2,

k∈K

where K is a fixed, finite, canonically declared test-vector set. K MUST be committed by hash
or generated deterministically from a public seed.

659



N3: Entrywise Max Norm

∥X∥∞ := max |Xij |.
i,j

Simple and deterministic.

N4: Spectral Commutator Proxy (CSF-Aware)

For workflows aligned with EY23, a proxy can be defined using filtered spectral summaries:

∥[A,B]∥spec_proxy := ∥Summary(F⋆([A,B]))∥,

where Summary and F⋆ are explicitly referenced artifacts (and must be deterministic). This
measure is allowed only if the EY23 reference is included in SpecID and interop predicates are
provided.

1.5 Tolerance Semantics

Fixed tolerance

ε ∈ R≥0 is fixed in SpecID.

Grid tolerance

ε ∈ {k · δε : 0 ≤ k ≤ Kε}
with δε,Kε fixed.

Rule. Floating “machine epsilon” tolerances are forbidden unless explicitly bound as a numeric
constant in SpecID.

1.6 Canonical Predicate Identifiers

To enable interoperability, EY27 standardizes predicate identifiers:

PredID := COMM-⟨Mode⟩-⟨Meas⟩-⟨ParamHash⟩.

ParamHash commits to (ε, P, σ, ϕ,K) as applicable.

Rule. If an artifact claims to use an EY27 commutation constraint in its Interop component,
it MUST reference the full PredID.

1.7 Deterministic Failure Codes (Mode/Measure Layer)

At minimum:
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH: products not defined on declared space.
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH: truncation level(s) incompatible.
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH: rounding/order differs from declared.

660



• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID: P fails idempotence/self-adjointness checks beyond
tolerance.

• FAIL_MEASURE_UNDEFINED: measure requires missing committed test vectors
or undefined summary.

• FAIL_COMMUTATION: predicate evaluates to FALSE.

1.8 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the normative commutation vocabulary for EY27: commutation modes
(exact, approximate, projected, graded, central-phase) and commutator measures (Frobenius,
operator-norm proxy, max norm, spectral proxy). It fixed tolerance semantics, canonical predicate
identifiers, and mode/measure-layer failure codes.
Chapter 3 next defines the EY27 artifact structure and SpecID binding for Gcomm: its in-
puts, outputs (predicate + optional constraint object), admissible families, numeric/truncation
requirements, and certificate payload.

2 Artifact Structure and SpecID Binding

2.1 Purpose

Chapters ??–1 fixed the meaning of commutation modes and measures. This chapter defines EY27
as a canonical generator artifact: it produces a commutation predicate (PredID), a deterministic
verification routine, and (optionally) a constructive constraint object that can be used by other
artifacts (EY24/EY25/EY26) to enforce the commutation condition.

2.2 Core Objects

EY27 binds commutation to declared objects under deterministic evaluation semantics.

Target objects. An EY27 instance declares:
(A,B) ∈ O ×O

(or a single target A commuted against a declared reference set B; see below), where O is a
declared operator class with canonical encoding rules.

Commutation contract. The contract is a predicate:
CompatComm(A,B) ∈ {TRUE,FALSE}

implemented as a deterministic routine.

2.3 Artifact Definition

Definition 2.1 (Commutant Generator). An EY27 artifact instance is a tuple:
Gcomm := (Mode, Meas, Θ, O, Trunc, NumericModel, RoutineSpec),

that induces:
PredID := COMM-⟨Mode⟩-⟨Meas⟩-⟨ParamHash⟩,

661



and a deterministic predicate evaluation routine

EvalGcomm(A,B) ∈ {TRUE,FALSE}.

Optionally, Gcomm may also output a constraint object K such that downstream artifacts can
enforce commutation by constraining admissible families or by adding penalties.

Rule (generator semantics). An EY27 publication MUST specify:
• the predicate form used (from Chapter 1),
• the exact measure computation semantics,
• the tolerance and any additional parameters Θ,
• and the deterministic routine EvalGcomm .

2.4 Parameter Tuple Θ
Θ collects mode/measure parameters:

Θ := (ε, P, σ, ϕ, K, EqPolicy),

where only the fields relevant to the chosen Mode/Meas are non-null.

EqPolicy. EqPolicy fixes:
• exact equality vs toleranced comparison,
• canonical rounding points before measuring,
• tie-break behavior for max operations,
• and serialization of intermediate objects if required for commitments.

Rule (anti-smuggling). All numeric parameters (including ε and ϕ) MUST be bounded and
on declared grids if not exact constants. If a parameter is not bound, the artifact MUST be
rejected.

2.5 Operator Class O and Encoding

EY27 MUST declare the operator class:

O := (Type, EncodingRule, AdjointSpec, CalcSpec).

Examples (informational).
• bounded matrices at truncation level N ,
• sparse operator encodings with deterministic multiplication semantics,
• operator families generated by EY23/EY24/EY25/EY26 references.

Rule. If operators are external (files, catalogs), they MUST be committed by hash (EY22
Appendix A.1).

662



2.6 RoutineSpec: Deterministic Verification Routine

The routine is not “implementation detail”; it is part of SpecID.

RoutineSpec fields

RoutineSpec := (RoutineID, MulOrder, ReduceOrder, CanonPoints, MeasAlg, ProjectorChecks).

RoutineID. A short identifier referencing a fully described routine (inline or committed by
hash). For baseline routines, EY27 defines a standard set.

MulOrder and ReduceOrder. Matrix multiplication order and reduction order MUST be
fixed:

• row-major vs column-major accumulation,
• deterministic associativity policy,
• deterministic max tie-break rules for entrywise measures.

CanonPoints. Canonical rounding points MUST be declared:
• before computing AB and BA,
• after computing the commutator object,
• before measuring.

MeasAlg. Measure algorithm must be fixed (e.g. Frobenius via trace order, operator proxy
via fixed test vectors K).

ProjectorChecks. If P is present (Mode M3), checks MUST be fixed:

∥P 2 − P∥Meas ≤ εP , ∥P − P †∥
P Meas ≤ ε ,

P P

with εP fixed in Θ (or exact).

2.7 SpecID for EY27

ArtifactType. For EY27:
ArtifactType = COMM.

SpecID components (EY27 binding). The full SpecID tuple is:

SpecIDEY27 := (COMM, Mode, Meas, Θ, O, Trunc, NumericModel, RoutineSpec, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

TranscriptSpec (required)

Even if the artifact only outputs a boolean, EY27 requires commitments that bind the check
inputs and outputs:

• commitments to canonical encodings (or hashes) of A,B (or their references),

663



• commitment to the predicate parameters (Θ),
• commitment to the evaluation output and measured value(s).

Rule. If an EY27 result is cited inside another artifact (e.g. to restrict admissible families),
the referenced PredID MUST match the committed parameters.

2.8 Optional Output: Constraint Object K

EY27 MAY output a constraint object K (committed by hash) for downstream enforcement. Two
canonical forms are permitted:

K1: Penalty operator (VPO-ready). Provide a penalty Vcomm such that:

∥[A,B]∥Meas ≤ ε ⇐ ⟨X,VcommX⟩ small,

with explicit construction rules.

K2: Admissibility constraint (token-ready). Provide a constraint descriptor that restricts
admissible steps/operators to those satisfying the predicate (checked by verifier).

Rule. If K is provided, it MUST be fully specified by deterministic construction rules and
committed by hash.

2.9 Deterministic Failure Codes (Structure Layer)

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH
• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID
• FAIL_MEASURE_UNDEFINED
• FAIL_COMMUTATION

2.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined EY27 as a canonical generator artifact: it binds commutation mode and
measure, parameters, operator class, truncation and numeric semantics, and a deterministic
verification routine into SpecID. It introduced TranscriptSpec commitments and the optional
constraint object K for downstream enforcement.

664

grids and bounds, and FLOQ/LIOUV restrictions induced by Gcomm in a machine-checkable
way.

4 Admissible Families and Baseline Routines (COMM-0)

4.1 Purpose

EY27 must be usable as a constraint primitive across Vol. No. IV. That requires:
• admissible families (anti-smuggling bounds) for parameters and references,
• baseline deterministic routines that every verifier can implement,

668



• and a standard “reference profile” that other artifacts can cite.
This chapter defines those pieces and introduces the baseline profile COMM-0.

4.2 Admissible Family ACOMM

An EY27 instance is admissible only if its SpecID parameters lie in a declared admissible family.

Definition 4.1 (Admissible EY27 Instance). An EY27 instance is admissible if:
1. all parameters in Θ are bounded and canonically encoded,
2. all referenced objects (operators, projectors, test vectors) are inline or hash-committed,
3. Mode is one of the standardized modes {M1, . . . ,M5} or a declared extension mode,
4. Meas is one of {N1, . . . ,N4} or a declared extension measure,
5. RoutineSpec references a deterministic routine with fixed multiply/reduce/canonicalization

behavior,
6. truncation levels are fixed and consistent (or bridged deterministically via CrossNPolicy),
7. and all checks are deterministic under NumericModel.

Rule (anti-smuggling). Any EY27 instance with free continuous parameters, adaptive test-
vector sets, or unspecified evaluation order MUST be rejected.

4.3 Parameter Bounds and Grids

Tolerance grid

For toleranced modes (M2/M3b/M4/M5), ε MUST be:

ε ∈ {k · δε : 0 ≤ k ≤ Kε},

with δε,Kε fixed in SpecID, unless ε is a single fixed constant.

Phase grid (M5)

If ϕ is used: {
ϕ ∈ 2 }

πq : q ∈ {0, . . . , Q− 1} ,
Q

with Q fixed and bounded.

Projector tolerance grid (M3)

If projector checks are toleranced:

εP ∈ {k · δP : 0 ≤ k ≤ KP }.

Rule. All grids MUST be declared. Defaulting to “machine epsilon” is forbidden.

669



4.4 Baseline Routine Set

EY27 defines baseline routines RoutineID ∈ R0 that are universally implementable.

Routine COMM-R0: Direct Commutator + Frobenius (N1)

Inputs. (A,B) at truncation level N .

Steps (deterministic).
1. Canonicalize A,B (NumericModel).
2. Compute AB and BA using declared MulOrder and ReduceOrder.
3. Compute C := AB −BA.
4. Canonicalize C.
5. Compute m := ∥C∥F via trace ordering.
6. Return TRUE iff m ≤ ε (or m = 0 in M1).

Outputs. Measured value m, boolean output, and transcript commitments.

Routine COMM-R1: Entrywise Max (N3)

Same as COMM-R0, but measure is:

m := ∥C∥∞ = max |Cij |,
i,j

with deterministic tie-break rules:
• scan order (row-major) fixed,
• if equal maxima occur, select the first occurrence.

Routine COMM-R2: Operator Norm Proxy (N2)

Inputs. (A,B), a committed test-vector set K = {v1, . . . , vs}.

Steps.
1. Compute C := AB −BA deterministically.
2. For each vk in a fixed order, compute wk := Cvk.
3. Compute mk := ∥wk∥2 deterministically.
4. Set m := maxkmk with deterministic tie-break.
5. Return TRUE iff m ≤ ε.

Rule (test vectors). K MUST be committed by hash or generated from a public seed with a
deterministic generator.

670



Routine COMM-R3: Projected Commutator (M3)

Steps. Compute:
CP := P (AB −BA)P

then apply N1/N3/N2 measure as declared. Projector validity checks must be executed first:
∥P 2 − P∥ ≤ εP , ∥P − P †∥ ≤ εP .

If checks fail: FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID.

Routine COMM-R4: Central-Phase Search (M5)

Steps. For ϕ in the declared grid order:
C(ϕ) := AB − eiϕBA, m(ϕ) := ∥C(ϕ)∥Meas.

Choose ϕ⋆ by deterministic minimization with tie-break (smallest grid index), and accept if
m(ϕ⋆) ≤ ε. If the token fixes ϕ instead of searching, this routine is not used.

Rule. Search order and tie-break MUST be explicit. Otherwise: FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

4.5 COMM-0 Reference Profile (Baseline)

COMM-0 is the conservative baseline profile for EY27, analogous to FLOQ-0 and LIOUV-0.

COMM-0 Fixes

COMM-0 fixes:
• allowed modes: M1 and M2 only,
• allowed measures: N1 or N3 only,
• routines: COMM-R0 (N1) or COMM-R1 (N3),
• truncation: single level N0 (or an explicit finite list with CrossNPolicy=none),
• tolerance: fixed ε (grid-tolerance allowed but must be fixed),
• canonicalization points: before products, after commutator, before measuring.

Rule. COMM-0 forbids projectors (M3), graded commutation (M4), and phase commutation
(M5) unless an explicit non-baseline profile is declared.

4.6 Using EY27 to Restrict Other Artifacts (Normative Patterns)

EY27 is most valuable when used to restrict admissible families elsewhere.

Pattern P1: Restricting EY26 Tokens

A token may require:
∀j, Comm(Uj , B) = TRUE

for a declared B (symmetry generator). This becomes part of ASteps for EY26, and the token
verifier must evaluate the referenced PredID for each step operator.

671



Rule. If an EY26 token claims an EY27 restriction, it MUST:
• reference PredID,
• define the set of step objects that are checked,
• define whether checks are per-step or per-period,
• and ensure all checks are deterministic and committed.

Pattern P2: Restricting EY25 Generators

An EY25 generator may require:

[H,B] = 0 or ∥[H,B]∥ ≤ ε,

as a membership condition for AG.

Pattern P3: Certifying Interop Stability

Interop predicates may require commutation stability under reduction or transport:

Comm(A,B) = TRUE ⇒ Comm(R(A), R(B)) = TRUE

or an explicitly weakened version. Such implications MUST be declared and checked (not
assumed).

4.7 Deterministic Failure Codes (Admissibility Layer)

At minimum:
• FAIL_CONSTRAINT: parameter bounds/grids violated.
• FAIL_ROUTINE_UNKNOWN: RoutineID not recognized and not provided by

committed definition.
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM: routine requires unspecified order/tie-break.
• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID: projector checks fail (if used).
• FAIL_COMMUTATION: predicate evaluates to FALSE.

4.8 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined admissible EY27 instances ACOMM, fixed bounded parameter grids, intro-
duced baseline deterministic routines (COMM-R0..R4), and defined the conservative reference
profile COMM-0. It also specified normative patterns for using EY27 to restrict EY26 tokens
and EY25 generators and to support interop stability claims.
Chapter 5 next specifies certificate payload and verifier checks for EY27: how commutation
results are committed, how routines are replayed, and how PredIDs are validated for downstream
composition.

5 Certificate and Verifier: PredID, Replay, and Acceptance

5.1 Purpose

EY27 must be citeable as a constraint artifact. That requires more than “TRUE/FALSE”: the
publication must bind the exact predicate meaning (PredID), the routine used to evaluate it, the
measured values, and the deterministic replay path.
This chapter specifies:

• the certificate payload πCOMM for EY27,
• deterministic verifier checks for acceptance,
• transcript commitments for commutation evaluations,
• and required failure codes.

EY27 certificates follow EY22 canonical certificate encoding (CCE) conventions and include
commutation-specific fields.

5.2 Certificate Object πCOMM

Rule. An EY27 publication MUST include a certificate πCOMM with the following canonical
content.

Header (required)

• artifact type: COMM

• artifact symbol: Gcomm

• PredID
• Version
• Certificate schema identifier (EY22-CCE)

SpecID (required)

The full SpecID tuple MUST be embedded:
SpecIDEY27 := (COMM, Mode, Meas, Θ, O, Trunc, NumericModel, RoutineSpec, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Committed Inputs (required)

πCOMM MUST commit to:
• canonical encoding or hash-commitment of A and B (or of their references and deterministic

reconstruction rules),
• the parameter tuple Θ (including ε, P, σ, ϕ,K,EqPolicy with nulls explicit),
• truncation configuration (levels, basis, cut rule, boundary rule),
• NumericModel (rounding points, multiplication/reduction order, tolerances),
• RoutineSpec (RoutineID and all routine-critical settings),

673



• any external objects: projector P , test vector set K, EY23 references (if measure N4),
committed by hash.

Committed Outputs (required)

πCOMM MUST commit to:
• measured commutator value(s) m (and, if applicable, ϕ⋆ for M5 search),
• boolean predicate outcome b ∈ {TRUE,FALSE},
• transcript commitments Tx as required by TranscriptSpec,
• deterministic failure code if evaluation fails.

Optional Constraint Object K (if published)

If a constraint object K is provided (Chapter 3), the certificate MUST include:
• canonical encoding or hash-commitment of K,
• deterministic construction rules (inline or committed by hash),
• statement of how K is intended to be used (penalty vs admissibility restriction).

5.3 PredID Computation (Normative)

PredID is the canonical identifier for commutation semantics.

Definition.
PredID := COMM-⟨Mode⟩-⟨Meas⟩-⟨ParamHash⟩,

where ParamHash is t(he hash of the canonical encoding of all commutation parameters: )
ParamHash := Hash Enc(Θ)∥Enc(O)∥Enc(Trunc)∥Enc(NumericModel)∥Enc(RoutineSpec) .

Rule. A verifier MUST recompute PredID from SpecID and reject if it does not match the
published PredID (REJECT_PREDID_MISMATCH).

5.4 Verifier Contract

A verifier consumes πCOMM and returns:

{ACCEPT,REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗}.

Rule. Verification MUST be deterministic under NumericModel and MUST not depend on
producer identity or runtime secrets.

5.5 Required Verifier Checks (Normative)

C1: Structural Validity (EY22-CCE)

Parse canonical certificate encoding and confirm all required fields exist. Failure: REJECT_MALFORMED.

674



C2: SpecID Completeness and Consistency

• ArtifactType = COMM,
• Mode, Meas, Θ, O, NumericModel, RoutineSpec are present,
• Trunc present if required by operator encodings,
• TranscriptSpec present and valid.

Failure: REJECT_SPECID_MISSING, REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH.

C3: PredID Recompute and Match

Recompute PredID and compare. Failure: REJECT_PREDID_MISMATCH.

C4: No Hidden Inputs (Commitment Integrity)

• all external objects are hash-committed and match,
• all operator references resolve deterministically,
• test vectors K or EY23 references exist if required.

Failure: FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH, REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT.

C5: Admissibility Check ACOMM

Verify bounds and grids:
• ε on declared grid or fixed constant,
• ϕ on declared grid if used,
• projector tolerances on declared grids if used,
• RoutineID recognized or committed definition supplied,
• canonical encoding is in normal form (nulls explicit).

Failure: FAIL_CONSTRAINT, FAIL_ROUTINE_UNKNOWN.

C6: Domain/Truncation Validity

• check products AB, BA are defined under CalcSpec,
• check truncation levels and basis are consistent with SpecID,
• for multi-level truncation, apply CrossNPolicy deterministically.

Failure: FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH, FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

C7: Routine Replay and Measurement

Execute the declared routine (COMM-R0.. or committed routine) deterministically:
• apply canonicalization points,

675



• compute commutator object (or graded/projected/phase variant),
• compute measure value(s) m,
• apply EqPolicy to decide b.

Failure:
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM if required tie-breaks/order not fixed,
• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID if P validation fails,
• FAIL_MEASURE_UNDEFINED if measure prerequisites missing,
• FAIL_COMMUTATION if predicate returns FALSE.

C8: Transcript Commitment Check

Recompute transcript commitments per TranscriptSpec and compare to published:

Tx(replay) =? Tx(published).

Failure: FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

C9: Optional Constraint Object Verification

If K is published:
• verify commitment hash for K,
• verify deterministic construction rules (if constructive),
• verify K usage declaration is consistent (penalty vs admissibility).

Failure: FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH, FAIL_CONSTRAINT.

5.6 Acceptance Rule

Rule. A verifier returns ACCEPT iff:
• C1–C6 pass,
• the declared routine executes deterministically,
• transcript commitments match,
• and the published boolean output matches replay output.

If the predicate output is FALSE, the artifact may still be well-formed but it does not certify
commutation; in that case the verifier returns FAIL_COMMUTATION (not ACCEPT).

5.7 Required Failure Codes

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING

676



• REJECT_SPECID_MISMATCH
• REJECT_PREDID_MISMATCH
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_CONSTRAINT
• FAIL_ROUTINE_UNKNOWN
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH
• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID
• FAIL_MEASURE_UNDEFINED
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_COMMUTATION
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH

validity, SpecID completeness, PredID recomputation, commitment integrity, admissibility

It also defined acceptance rules and required failure codes, making EY27 citeable as a strict

6 Interop Declarations (Mini): How COMM Constraints Com-
pose

6.1 Purpose

EY27 is intended to be a constraint layer that other artifacts can cite. This chapter instantiates
the EY22 interoperability framework for commutation constraints:

• how EY27 PredIDs are referenced inside Interop components,
• how commutation constraints restrict EY26 admissible step families and EY25 admissible

generator families,
• and what stability requirements apply under EY23 filtering, EY24 validity, EY28 transport,

and EY29 reduction.

677



Rule. Interop is a contract. If an artifact claims it is “symmetry-compatible” or “commutant-
preserving”, it MUST reference a concrete EY27 PredID and MUST provide a checkable
compatibility predicate under the declared NumericModel.

6.2 Interop Component in SpecID (EY27 Requirement)

Every artifact in EY23–EY30 that claims a commutation constraint MUST include an interop
entry: ( )

Interop ∋ COMM-Ref = PredID, CommUse, CommCheckScope .

Required fields.
• COMM-Ref: full PredID and commitment hash of πCOMM (or the SpecID hash).
• CommUse: how the constraint is used: admissibility, penalty, certificate, or

annotation.
• CommCheckScope: where checks are applied: per-step, per-period, final-only, or an

explicit tick set.

Rule. If CommUse = admissibility or certificate, then CommCheckScope MUST be
explicit and MUST be enforced by verifiers.

6.3 Compatibility Predicates (EY27 Perspective)

EY27 defines minimal predicate IDs for interoperability. All are deterministic under Numeric-
Model.

COMM → FLOQ: Restricting Program Tokens

A common claim is: “this token respects symmetry B”. Formally, a token UF is commutant-
compatible if required step operators commute (or approximately commute) with a declared
reference B under a declared PredID.

Predicate Compat(1)
27,26 (binding).

Compat(1)
27,26 := (EIF the token’s Interop includes COMM-Ref = PredID and matches the committed πCOMM).

Predicate Compat(2)
27,26 (scope).

Compat(2)
27,26 := (EIF CommCheckScope is explicit and refers to a deterministic set of checked step objects).

Predicate Compat(3)
27,26 (replay check).

Compat(3)
27,26 := (EIF the EY26 verifier evaluates the COMM predicate at the declared scope under aligned NumericModel/Trunc).

Compatibility status.
Compat(EY27,EY26) := Compat(1)

27,26 ∧ Compat(2)
27,26 ∧ Compat(3)

27,26.

If TRUE, mark OK∗.

678



Failure codes. FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE, FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH,
FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH, FAIL_COMMUTATION.

COMM → LIOUV: Restricting Audit-Native Generators

EY25 generators often claim invariant preservation or symmetry. EY27 provides a canonical way
to bind that claim.

Predicate Compat(1)
27,25 (generator restriction).

Compat(1)
27,25 := (EIF EY25’s admissible generator family AG references PredID and declares what commutes).

Predicate Compat(2)
27,25 (object of commutation).

Compat(2)
27,25 := (EIF EY25 declares whether COMM applies to H, to L, to noise terms, or to induced step maps).

Predicate Compat(3)
27,25 (stability under evolution). For invariance claims, the workflow

must declare what is preserved:

[A,B] = 0 ⇒ [L(A), B] = 0 (or a toleranced variant),

and provide a deterministic check routine at declared checkpoints.

Compatibility status.

Compat(EY27,EY25) := Compat(1)
27,25 ∧ Compat(2)

27,25 ∧ Compat(3)
27,25.

If TRUE, mark OK∗.

COMM ↔ CSF: Filtered Symmetry and Commutation Probing

EY23 may operate on operators or derived commutators.

Predicate Compat(1)
27,23 (measure dependence). If EY27 uses the spectral proxy measure

(N4), then:

Compat(1)
27,23 := (EIF EY27 SpecID includes an EY23 reference and NumericModel alignment is declared).

Otherwise, compatibility is optional.

Predicate Compat(2)
27,23 (filter commutation stability, optional). If a workflow claims that

filtering preserves commutation:

Comm(A,B)⇒ Comm(F⋆(A), F⋆(B)),

it MUST include a deterministic check routine (usually at truncation N and checkpoint set).
Failure: FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED.

679



COMM ↔ VPO: Commutation-Enforced Validity

EY24 validity penalties can encode symmetry constraints.

Predicate Compat(1)
27,24 (penalty binding). If EY24 claims to penalize commutation violation,

it MUST:
• reference PredID,
• declare the penalty construction (e.g. Vcomm = C†C with C encoding commutator residual),
• and commit to construction rules.

Predicate Compat(2)
27,24 (equivalence non-claim). The existence of a penalty does not imply

exact commutation. If a claim needs commutation, it must still cite a COMM predicate check,
or explicitly define what “valid” means in terms of commutation residual.

COMM ↔ INTW: Transport of Symmetry Constraints

Transport can preserve commutation only under explicit semantics.

Predicate Compat(1)
27,28 (transported constraint). If T1→2 transports A1 7→ A2, B1 7→ B2,

then a workflow may claim:
Comm(A1, B1)⇒ Comm(A2, B2).

This is permitted only if the workflow declares:
• whether transport is unitary/isometric/generalized,
• how adjoints/inverses are computed deterministically,
• and a deterministic check routine at declared truncation.

Failure. FAIL_CALC_MISMATCH, FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH, FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED.

COMM ↔ CGR: Reduction and Symmetry

Reduction often weakens commutation. Therefore, any claim of preservation MUST be explicit.

Predicate Compat(1)
27,29 (reduced commutation). A workflow may declare either:

• strong: Comm(A,B)⇒ Comm(R(A), R(B)),
• weak: ∥[R(A), R(B)]∥ ≤ g(∥[A,B]∥) for a declared deterministic bound function g.

In either case, it MUST provide a deterministic check routine and tolerances.

7 COMM-0 Reference Instance, Publication Boundary, and Non-
Claims

7.1 Purpose

This chapter closes EY27 by:
• providing a concrete COMM-0 reference SpecID template (a stable meaning of “commuta-

tion constraint artifact”),
• fixing what must be published for a valid EY27 artifact,
• stating explicit non-claims (what EY27 does not guarantee),
• and recording licensing intent consistent with Vol. No. IV.

7.2 COMM-0 Reference Instance (Template)

COMM-0 is the conservative baseline profile defined in Chapter 4. The following template fixes
a “default” SpecID for universal verifiers.

COMM-0 profile choices.
• Mode ∈ {M1,M2},

681



• Meas ∈ {N1,N3},
• RoutineID ∈ {COMM-R0,COMM-R1},
• single truncation level N0 (or an explicit finite list with CrossNPolicy=none),
• explicit constant ε (or an ε-grid with fixed δε,Kε).

Reference SpecID (COMM-0)

SpecID_EY27_COMM0 :=
(
ArtifactType = COMM,

Mode = "M2-approx" # or "M1-exact" if eps=0 exact under numeric model
Meas = "N1-frobenius", # or "N3-max"

Theta = {
eps: 1e-10, # fixed (or grid: {delta:..., K:...})
P: null, # COMM-0 forbids projectors
sigma: "-", # default commutator (COMM-0 forbids graded variants)
phi: null, # COMM-0 forbids phase commutation
K: null, # COMM-0 forbids operator-norm proxy vectors
EqPolicy: {
compare: "<= eps",
canon_before_products: true,
canon_after_commutator: true,
canon_before_measure: true,
tie_break: "first-in-scan"

}
},

OperatorClass O = {
Type: "finite-matrix",
EncodingRule: "canonical",
AdjointSpec: "dagger",
CalcSpec: "matmul"

},

Trunc = {
Basis: Hash(basis0), # or inline if small
CutRule: "cut0",
BoundaryRule: "boundary0",
N: 1024,
CrossNPolicy: "none"

},

NumericModel = {
arithmetic: "det-float-or-fixed",
rounding: { mode:"nearest", precision:64 },
matmul: { order:"row-major", accumulate:"sequential" },
canon: { rule:"normalize-encoding" },
tolerances: { eps_step: 0.0 } # COMM-0 recommends exact canon after each stage

682



},

RoutineSpec = {
RoutineID: "COMM-R0", # (N1) or "COMM-R1" (N3)
MulOrder: "row-major",
ReduceOrder: "sequential",
CanonPoints: ["before-products","after-commutator","before-measure"],
MeasAlg: "trace-ordered", # for N1; or "entrywise-scan" for N3
ProjectorChecks: null

},

TranscriptSpec = {
CommitType: "summary", # summary is allowed: commits to A-hash, B-hash, m, b
HashAlg: "sha256",
SerializeRule: "EY22-CCE",
CommitRate: "single", # one commitment per evaluation
ChainRule: "none"

},

Cert = {
schema:"EY22-CCE",
required_checks:["C1","C2","C3","C4","C5","C6","C7","C8"]

},

Interop = {
allowed_forms:["C1","C4"], # algebraic composition and superoperator embedding (informative)
references:{}

},

Version = "VID-2026-02"
)

Rule. If a COMM-0 instance forbids a feature (projectors, phase, graded), the corresponding
Θ fields MUST be explicitly null. Omitting them is not allowed.

7.3 Publication Boundary (Normative)

Rule (what must be public). An EY27 publication MUST include:
• full SpecIDEY27,
• PredID and the rule used to compute it (ParamHash construction),
• canonical encodings or hash commitments for A and B (or references + deterministic

reconstruction),
• full Θ including all nulls explicitly,
• truncation and NumericModel (including multiply/reduce order and canonicalization

points),
• RoutineSpec (RoutineID and all routine-critical settings),
• measured value(s) m and boolean outcome b,

683



• transcript commitment(s) Tx (at least one),
• and certificate πCOMM with required checks (Chapter 5).

Rule (no hidden commutation objects). If B is “a symmetry generator”, it must be
published or committed like any other operator. “Known symmetry” is not an input.

7.4 Non-Claims (Explicit)

EY27 explicitly does not claim:

NC1: Analytic Commutation in the Infinite Limit

Passing a commutation check at truncation N does not imply exact commutation in the full
infinite-dimensional system. Any such limit statement must be made separately and is outside
EY27.

NC2: Uniqueness of the Symmetry

If [A,B] = 0, EY27 does not claim that B is the only symmetry, or that the commutant is fully
characterized.

NC3: Physical Meaning

Commutation constraints may encode physical symmetries, but EY27 does not assert physical
correctness. It asserts only that the declared predicate holds under declared numeric/truncation
semantics.

NC4: Robustness to Adversarial Encoding

EY27 reduces smuggling by bounds and commitments, but does not guarantee adversarial
robustness beyond the declared verifier checks.

NC5: Preservation Under Transformations Unless Declared

Reduction (EY29), transport (EY28), filtering (EY23), and audit evolution (EY25) do not
automatically preserve commutation. Preservation must be explicitly declared and checked.

7.5 Licensing Intent (Vol. No. IV)

The specification of EY27 (SpecID, PredID rules, baseline routines, verifier checks) is intended
to remain publicly readable. Implementations and operator catalogs may be licensed under
project-chosen terms, but:

auditability may not be removed.

Rule (no audit stripping). No distribution or license arrangement may claim EY27 compli-
ance while omitting SpecID binding, commitments, and verifier-replay rules.

684



7.6 Chapter Summary

This chapter provided a COMM-0 reference SpecID template, fixed the publication boundary
(what must be public and committed), stated explicit non-claims (no infinite-limit guarantees,
no uniqueness, no physical meaning, no implicit robustness, no automatic preservation), and
recorded licensing intent consistent with Vol. No. IV: the spec remains auditable and public;
implementations may vary, but auditability is mandatory.

Next. With EY27 complete, Vol. No. IV proceeds to EY28: the Regime Intertwiner T1→2,
which standardizes how operators and constraints are transported across regimes while preserving

8 Worked Examples (Non-Normative): How COMM Constraints
Are Used

8.1 Purpose

Chapters ??–7 defined EY27 normatively. This chapter is non-normative: it illustrates typical
ways commutation constraints appear in Vol. No. IV workflows, and how to publish them so
that third parties can replay checks deterministically.

Note. Examples are schematic. They are valid only if all referenced objects are canonically
encoded or hash-committed and NumericModel/Truncation are fixed.

8.2 Example 1: Symmetry Constraint on a Hamiltonian (EY25-Ready)

Goal. Publish the claim that a Hamiltonian H respects a symmetry generator B:

∥[H,B]∥F ≤ ε.

EY27 instance. Choose:

Mode = M2, Meas = N1, ε = 10−10, RoutineID = COMM-R0.

Commit to H and B encodings (or their hashes), fix truncation N , and publish πCOMM.

How EY25 uses it. EY25 includes in AG an admissibility clause:

PredIDHB must return TRUE.

If an EY25 generator family changes H, it must re-commit and re-check at declared checkpoints.

8.3 Example 2: Token Restriction (EY26 Per-Step Symmetry)

Goal. Publish a token UF = ∏m
j=1 Uj where each step respects the same symmetry B:

∀j, ∥[Uj , B]∥∞ ≤ ε.

685



EY27 instance. Choose:

Mode = M2, Meas = N3, RoutineID = COMM-R1.

Bind B by hash in the PredID parameters.

How EY26 encodes it. In EY26 Interop:
• COMM-Ref = PredID,
• CommUse = admissibility,
• CommCheckScope = per-step.

The EY26 verifier evaluates the COMM predicate for each step operator Uj against B, using the
same truncation and NumericModel.

8.4 Example 3: Projected Symmetry (Subspace Invariance)

Goal. Require commutation only on a declared subspace (e.g. a “valid” or “physical” subspace):

∥P [H,B]P∥F ≤ ε.

EY27 instance (non-baseline). Choose:

Mode = M3b, Meas = N1, RoutineID = COMM-R3.

Publish P (or commit by hash), and publish projector validity checks:

∥P 2 − P∥F ≤ εP , ∥P − P †∥F ≤ εP .

How EY24 can embed it. EY24 can define a penalty operator that punishes leaving the
projected commutant:

Vcomm := C†C, C := P (HB −BH)P,
with deterministic construction and truncation binding. (Still: penalties do not imply exact
commutation outside P .)

8.5 Example 4: Central-Phase Commutation for Unitary Steps

Goal. Allow commutation up to a central phase:

∥UB − eiϕBU∥Meas ≤ ε.

EY27 instance (non-baseline). Ch{oose:
2 }

Mode = M5, ϕ ∈ πq
, RoutineID = COMM-R4.

Q

Two patterns are valid:
• fixed ϕ: ϕ is part of SpecID and checked directly,
• searched ϕ⋆: routine searches grid in fixed order and commits ϕ⋆.

686



8.6 Example 5: “Commutation Stability Under Reduction” (EY29)

Goal. Claim that reduction R preserves symmetry:

∥[A,B]∥ ≤ ε⇒ ∥[R(A), R(B)]∥ ≤ ε̃.

Declaration (required). The workflow must declare:
• the exact reduction placement (before/after canonicalization),
• whether R(B) is computed by the same R or by a specialized map,
• the relation between tolerances (ε̃ fixed or via a declared bound function g).

Then it must provide a deterministic routine that checks both predicates at the declared truncation
and NumericModel.

8.7 Example 6: “Commutation Stability Under Transport” (EY28)

Goal. Claim that an intertwiner transports a symmetry:

[A1, B1] = 0⇒ [A2, B2] = 0, A2 = TA1T
−1, B2 = TB1T

−1.

Declaration (required). The workflow must declare:
• whether T−1 or T † is used (unitary vs generalized),
• how T and inverses/adjoints are computed deterministically,
• truncation alignment across regimes,
• and the exact EY27 predicate used before and after transport.

8.8 Chapter Summary

This non-normative chapter illustrated how EY27 commutation constraints are used in practice:
symmetry constraints on Hamiltonians (EY25), per-step token restrictions (EY26), projected
commutation (M3), central-phase commutation (M5), and stability claims under reduction
(EY29) and transport (EY28). In each case, the key principle remains: the commutation meaning
must be bound to SpecID and replayable by independent verifiers.

Next. Proceed to EY28: Regime Intertwiner T1→2 (transport across regimes), which will inherit
and reuse EY27 constraints as transported predicates with explicit preservation checks.

Chapter 28

EY28: Regime Intertwiner T1→2
Canonical Operator Artifacts for QFC

Enter Yourname

Abstract
This whitepaper defines the Regime Intertwiner T1→2, a canonical artifact
for transporting operators, states, and constraints between two spectral
regimes (or layers) while preserving explicitly declared invariants. Unlike
informal “change of basis” or “mapping” narratives, EY28 binds transport
semantics to SpecID: the mapping type (unitary, isometric, partial, or
generalized), the required adjoint/inverse behavior, truncation alignment
across regimes, and deterministic verification routines.

T1→2 is intended as the bridge artifact for Vol. No. IV workflows: it allows canonical spectral
filters (EY23), validity penalties (EY24), audit-native Liouvillians (EY25), program tokens
(EY26), and commutation constraints (EY27) to be moved across layers without ambiguity,
producing interop certificates that verifiers can replay deterministically.

1 Motivation, Scope, and Intuition: Transport Without Smug-
gling

1.1 Motivation: “Map It to Another Regime” Is Usually Undefined

Operator workflows often rely on statements like:

“move this operator to another basis/regime” or “transport the constraint to the
next layer”.

But without a formal transport artifact, such statements hide:
• what the two regimes (1) and (2) actually are (spaces, truncations, encodings),
• whether the map is unitary, isometric, partial, or merely heuristic,
• what replaces the inverse if the map is not invertible,
• how adjoints are treated and what “preservation” means numerically,
• how truncation levels align (or fail) across regimes,
• and how a third party can verify that transport did not change the claim.

Vol. No. IV exists to remove hidden semantics. Therefore, “transport” must become an auditable
artifact.
EY28 defines T1→2: a canonical regime intertwiner that binds transport semantics to SpecID
and enables deterministic verification.



1.2 What EY28 Defines

EY28 defines:
• a transport artifact T1→2 between two declared regimes,
• a normative vocabulary of transport semantics (unitary, isometric, partial, generalized),
• canonical pushforward/pullback forms and when each is permitted,
• truncation alignment policies (same-N , mapped-N , multi-N with CrossNPolicy),
• preservation predicates for invariants (spectral class, trace, positivity, commutation),
• certificate and verifier routines for deterministic replay,
• interoperability mini-declarations for composing transported artifacts in Vol. No. IV.

1.3 Scope

In-scope.
• Transport of operators A1 on regime 1 into operators A2 on regime 2.
• Transport of states/objects X1 into X2.
• Transport of constraints (e.g. EY27 commutation predicates) into transported constraints

with explicit check routines.
• Deterministic verification under declared NumericModel and truncation policies.

Out-of-scope.
• “Learned” mappings without committed parameters and deterministic replay path.
• Heuristic embeddings that are not SpecID-bound and cannot be verified by third parties.
• Statements about infinite-dimensional equivalence without explicit truncation semantics.

1.4 Intuition: Regimes as Typed Spaces

A regime is not just a label; it is a typed execution/representation environment. EY28 treats
each regime as:

Rk := (Hk, Enck, Trunck, NumericModelk, CalcSpeck).

Regime examples (informational).
• H1 = full-resolution truncation, H2 = coarse-grained truncation.
• H1 = operator-on-states space, H2 = observable-space for Koopman export.
• H1 = “physical” subspace, H2 = “audit” space augmented with certificates.

Transport must specify how encodings and truncations relate. Otherwise, a map can silently
change the meaning of the computation.

689



1.5 Canonical Transport Forms

EY28 standardizes two canonical transport directions, mirroring EY22 C2.

Pushforward (operator transport)

Given an operator A1 in regime 1, define the transported operator A2 by:

A2 := T1→2A1 S2→1,

where S2→1 is the declared back-map (inverse, adjoint, pseudo-inverse, or left/right inverse as
specified).

Special cases.
• Unitary: S2→1 = T−1

1→2 = T †
1→2.

• Isometric: S2→1 = T †
1→2 (left inverse on the image).

• Generalized: S2→1 = T+
1→2 (a declared pseudo-inverse routine).

Pullback (observable/constraint transport)

For an observable g2 or constraint defined in regime 2, pull it back to regime 1 by:

g1 := S2→1 g2 T1→2,

with the same back-map semantics.

Rule. Every EY28 instance MUST declare both the forward map T1→2 and the back-map
semantics S2→1. If S2→1 is not unique (e.g. pseudo-inverse), the selection routine MUST be
deterministic.

1.6 Why a Dedicated Artifact (Not “Just a Basis Change”)

A basis change is only one transport subtype. EY28 is broader:
• regime changes can include truncation change, coarse-graining, projection, augmentation,

or encoding change,
• transport may be partial: only a subspace or subset of operators is meaningful in the target

regime,
• constraints must be transported as checkable predicates, not as informal claims.

Therefore, T1→2 is treated as a first-class auditable object with its own SpecID, certificate, and
verifier checks.

1.7 Design Goals (Normative)

G1: Deterministic Transport

Transport MUST be replayable: given committed inputs and NumericModel, every verifier
computes the same transported object.

690



G2: No Smuggling Across Regimes

Transport must not be used to hide changes. Any change of truncation, tolerance, or calculus
semantics must be explicit in SpecID.

G3: Preservation Is Declared, Not Assumed

Invariants are preserved only if a preservation predicate is declared and checked. Otherwise, no
preservation claim is implied.

G4: Composability Across Vol. No. IV

EY28 must compose with:
• EY23 filtering (transporting H and filter inputs),
• EY24 penalties (transporting V and constraint operators),
• EY25 Liouvillian evolution (transporting generators or trajectories),
• EY26 tokens (transporting step operators or executed trajectories),
• EY27 commutation predicates (transporting constraints with explicit checks),
• EY29 coarse-graining (explicitly declaring when transport is itself a reduction).

1.8 Chapter Summary

This chapter motivated EY28: transport is usually informal and hides semantics. EY28 defines the
regime intertwiner T1→2, a SpecID-bound artifact that makes mapping between regimes auditable
and deterministic. It introduced regimes as typed spaces, canonical pushforward/pullback forms,
the requirement to declare back-map semantics, and the normative design goals: deterministic
transport, anti-smuggling, declared preservation, and composability.
Chapter 2 next defines the normative transport semantics classes (unitary, isometric, partial,
generalized), the allowed back-map types, and the exact preservation predicate forms used
throughout EY28.

2 Transport Semantics Classes and Preservation Predicates

2.1 Purpose

EY28 must remove ambiguity from the word “transport”. This chapter defines:
• normative transport semantics classes (unitary, isometric, partial, generalized),
• the allowed back-map types S2→1,
• preservation predicate vocabulary (what can be claimed preserved and how it is checked),
• and deterministic failure codes for semantic mismatch.

Rule. Every EY28 instance MUST declare a semantics class SemClass and a back-map type
BackMapType. If either is missing, the artifact is invalid.

691



2.2 Semantics Class SemClass

Let T := T1→2 be the forward map and S := S2→1 the declared back-map. Let H1,H2 be the
regime spaces.

S1: Unitary Transport

Definition. SemClass = UNIT if:

T †T = IH1 , TT † = IH2 ,

and the back-map is fixed as:
S = T−1 = T †.

Implications (informational). Unitary transport preserves:
• inner products and norms,
• spectrum (up to multiplicity in finite truncation),
• trace and positivity under conjugation.

But such preservation claims are still required to be declared if they are used in interop certificates.

S2: Isometric Transport

Definition. SemClass = ISO if:
T †T = IH1 ,

but TT † ̸= IH2 in general. The natural back-map is:

S = T †,

which is a left inverse on the image of T .

Interpretation. Regime 1 embeds into regime 2 as a subspace. Transport can preserve
structure on the embedded image, but not globally.

S3: Partial/Projected Transport

Definition. SemClass = PART if transport is defined only on a declared subset:

D1 ⊆ H1 and/or D2 ⊆ H2,

typically via projectors P1, P2. Transport obligations are stated only for objects restricted to
these domains.

Canonical form. A projected transport may declare:

T := P2 T̃ P1, S := P1 S̃ P2,

with explicit projector validity checks (idempotence/self-adjointness) and deterministic routines.

692



Rule. If SemClass = PART, the artifact MUST publish the domain declarations (projectors or
explicit admissible sets), otherwise claims of preservation are meaningless.

S4: Generalized Transport (Non-Invertible / Pseudo-Inverse)

Definition. SemClass = GEN if T is not invertible and the back-map is a declared generalized
inverse:

S := T+,

computed by a deterministic routine (e.g. truncated SVD with fixed thresholds).

Rule (pseudo-inverse determinism). If a pseudo-inverse is used, the artifact MUST declare:
• the algorithm (e.g. SVD) and ordering conventions,
• threshold/grid policy for singular values,
• truncation and rounding policies,
• and tie-breaks for degenerate singular values.

Otherwise, reject with FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

2.3 Back-Map Types BackMapType

EY28 standardizes the allowed back-map types:

B1: Adjoint

S = T †.

Allowed for UNIT and ISO, and sometimes PART (with explicit domain restrictions).

B2: Inverse

S = T−1.

Allowed only if the inverse exists in the declared truncation and is computed deterministically.

B3: Pseudo-Inverse

S = T+.

Allowed only for GEN (and sometimes PART) with explicit deterministic routine.

B4: Left/Right Inverse on Image

Declare S such that:

ST = IH1 (left inverse) or TS = IH2 (right inverse),

only on a declared image/domain. Requires PART semantics with explicit domain declaration.

693



Rule. If BackMapType is not † or (−1), the artifact MUST include a RoutineSpec for computing
S.

2.4 Preservation Predicate Vocabulary

Preservation is declared as explicit predicates. EY28 standardizes a minimal vocabulary.

Definition 2.1 (Preservation Predicate). A preservation predicate is a deterministic boolean
condition:

Preserveα(T ; inputs) ∈ {TRUE,FALSE},
with explicit tolerance and check routines under declared NumericModel(s).

P1: Inner Product Preservation

⟨Tx, Ty⟩2 ≈ ⟨x, y⟩1
checked on a fixed test set V (committed by hash or deterministic seed). Exact for UNIT/ISO in
exact arithmetic; toleranced otherwise.

P2: Norm Preservation (Isometry Test)

∥Tx∥2 ≈ ∥x∥1
on V, with explicit tolerance.

P3: Operator Conjugation Consistency

For a declared operator family F :
A2 =? TA1S

checked either exactly (finite exact arithmetic) or within tolerance using a declared matrix/operator
norm.

P4: Spectrum-Class Preservation (Filter-Aware)

For workflows that care about spectral classes (EY23), define:

Class(A1) =? Class(A2)

under a declared classifier, typically based on committed spectral summaries or canonical filters.
This predicate is permitted only if the classifier is committed and deterministic.

P5: Trace / Positivity Preservation (Density-Aware)

For states ρ1 7→ ρ2 = Tρ1S:
Tr(ρ2) ≈ Tr(ρ1), ρ2 ⪰ 0,

checked with explicit tolerance and positivity test routine (deterministic eigenvalue threshold
grid).

694



P6: Commutation Preservation (EY27-Aware)

If Comm(A1, B1) = TRUE under a declared EY27 PredID, then a workflow may claim:

Comm(A2, B2) = TRUE, A2 = TA1S, B2 = TB1S,

but only if it declares:
• the transported PredID (or the transported objects and re-check under an EY27 instance

in regime 2),
• truncation alignment,
• and explicit tolerance semantics.

Rule. No commutation preservation is implied by default, even for UNIT transport, unless
explicitly declared and checked.

2.5 Tolerance and Test-Set Rules

Several preservation predicates rely on finite test sets V or F .

Rule (test sets). Any finite test set used for preservation MUST be:
• explicitly listed (if small), or
• committed by hash (if large), or
• generated deterministically from a public seed with a declared generator routine.

Otherwise: REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT.

Rule (tolerance binding). All tolerances used in preservation predicates MUST be explicit
constants or quantized grids fixed in SpecID.

2.6 Deterministic Failure Codes (Semantics Layer)

At minimum:
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_SEMCLASS_MISSING
• REJECT_BACKMAP_MISSING
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH
• FAIL_PRESERVATION

695



2.7 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined normative transport semantics classes (UNIT, ISO, PART, GEN), allowed
back-map types (adjoint, inverse, pseudo-inverse, left/right inverse on image), and a standardized
vocabulary of preservation predicates (inner product, norm, conjugation consistency, spectrum-
class, trace/positivity, commutation). It fixed test-set and tolerance binding rules and introduced
semantics-layer failure codes.
Chapter 3 next defines the EY28 artifact structure and SpecID schema: how regimes are declared,
how T and S are encoded/committed, how truncation alignment is specified, and what certificates
are required for transported claims.

3 Artifact Structure and SpecID Schema

3.1 Purpose

Chapters 1–2 defined why transport must be auditable and fixed the semantics classes and
preservation predicates. This chapter defines EY28 as an artifact with a precise SpecID schema:

• how the two regimes are declared,
• how the forward map T1→2 and the back-map S2→1 are represented and committed,
• how truncation alignment is specified,
• how preservation claims are bound to check routines,
• and what transcript/certificate payload is required.

3.2 Regime Declarations

Each regime is a typed environment:
Rk := (Hk, Enck, Trunck, NumericModelk, CalcSpeck).

RegimeSpec tuple

EY28 standardizes a regime declaration object:
RegimeSpeck := (RegimeIDk, SpaceTypek, EncodingRulek, Trunck, NumericModelk, CalcSpeck).

Rule. Both RegimeSpec1 and RegimeSpec2 MUST appear in SpecID. A transport without
regime typing is invalid.

3.3 Map Objects T and S

Let:
T := T1→2, S := S2→1.

MapSpec tuple

EY28 represents each map by a MapSpec:
MapSpec(M) := (MapType, EncodingRule, AdjointSpec, InverseSpec, RoutineSpec).

696



MapType. At minimum one of:
• matrix-explicit (finite matrix in canonical encoding),
• sparse-linear (sparse operator with deterministic apply),
• factored (product of committed factors in a declared order),
• constructed (deterministic construction from committed data/rules).

EncodingRule. Must bind canonical serialization and hashing. If the map is external, it
MUST be committed by hash (EY22 Appendix A).

AdjointSpec / InverseSpec. Must declare whether adjoints/inverses are:
• computed explicitly and committed,
• computed by a deterministic routine,
• or not available (only allowed when SemClass declares it, e.g. PART with domain limits).

RoutineSpec. If S is a pseudo-inverse or generalized inverse, RoutineSpec MUST be present
and fully specified (Chapter 2).

Commitment Rules

Rule (map commitment). SpecID MUST bind map content by one of:
• inline canonical encoding (small maps),
• hash commitment to the encoded object,
• or hash commitment to a deterministic construction recipe + committed inputs.

Otherwise: REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT.

3.4 Transport Declaration Object

EY28 standardizes the transport declaration:

TransportDecl := (SemClass, BackMapType, PushPullForms, AlignPolicy, PreserveSet).

PushPullForms

Declare which forms are used:
• pushforward: A2 := TA1S,
• pullback: g1 := Sg2T ,
• or both.

Rule. If an artifact uses pushforward/pullback in later claims, the form MUST be declared
here.

697



AlignPolicy (Truncation Alignment Policy)

Truncation alignment is one of:
• same-N: both regimes use identical truncation N ,
• mapped-N: N2 = f(N1) with declared deterministic f ,
• multi-N: explicit finite lists N1 ∈ N1, N2 ∈ N2 with a declared CrossNPolicy,
• projected: transport defined only on declared projectors P1, P2 (PART semantics).

Rule. If AlignPolicy is not same-N, the policy MUST include all mapping rules and tie-breaks.
Otherwise: FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

PreserveSet

PreserveSet is a finite set of declared preservation predicates from Chapter 2:

PreserveSet ⊆ {P1, . . . ,P6}

plus any declared extensions (each with committed definition).

Rule. Only predicates listed in PreserveSet may be claimed preserved by this transport.
Anything else is non-claim.

3.5 SpecID for EY28

ArtifactType. For EY28:
ArtifactType = INTW.

SpecID components (EY28 binding). The full SpecID tuple is:

SpecIDEY28 := (INTW, RegimeSpec1, RegimeSpec2, MapSpec(T ), MapSpec(S), TransportDecl, NumericModelLink, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

NumericModelLink

Because two regimes may declare different NumericModels, EY28 includes a linking component:

NumericModelLink := (NMPolicy, Coercions, OrderFixes).

NMPolicy. One of:
• must-match: NumericModel1 = NumericModel2,
• coerce: a declared coercion rule exists,
• separate: computations are done in each regime separately with explicit cross-check rules.

Rule. If NMPolicy is coerce, the coercion routine MUST be deterministic and committed by
hash.

698



3.6 TranscriptSpec and Required Commitments

Transport is often used to justify downstream claims. Therefore EY28 requires transcript
commitments that bind:

• the committed representation (or construction recipe) of T and S,
• all regime declarations and truncation alignment policies,
• all preservation predicate results that are claimed,
• and any transported objects A2, B2, etc. when those objects are published as outputs.

Rule. If a downstream artifact claims to depend on transported content (e.g. “we applied
EY23 in regime 2 after transporting H”), the EY28 transcript commitments MUST be sufficient
to replay that transport.

3.7 Interop Component (Mini)

EY28 interop binds which artifacts are transported and how.

Required fields.
• TransportedArtifacts: list of artifact references whose objects are transported (EY23/EY24/EY25/EY26/EY27/EY29),
• FormsUsed: which pushforward/pullback forms were used per artifact,
• PreservationClaims: which predicates in PreserveSet are asserted for which transported

objects,
• CompatPredicates: predicate IDs (EY22 style) used to certify compatibility.

Rule. If an interop claim asserts preservation of commutation constraints, it MUST cite the
relevant EY27 PredID(s) and re-check routine(s).

3.8 Deterministic Failure Codes (Schema Layer)

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_PRESERVATION

699



3.9 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the EY28 artifact schema: typed regime declarations, committed map
specifications for T and S, a transport declaration object binding semantics class, back-map
type, push/pull forms, truncation alignment policy, and a finite preservation predicate set. It
also specified NumericModel linking, required transcript commitments, interop mini fields, and
schema-layer failure codes.
Chapter 4 next defines primitive composition forms and baseline routines for computing T , S,
transported objects, and preservation checks deterministically (INTW-0 reference profile).

4 Primitive Transport Forms and Baseline Routines (INTW-0)

4.1 Purpose

EY28 must be practically verifiable. That requires baseline routines that:
• compute transported objects deterministically,
• compute back-maps (if not explicitly provided) deterministically,
• evaluate preservation predicates on fixed test sets,
• and produce replayable transcript commitments.

This chapter defines primitive transport forms and introduces the conservative reference profile
INTW-0.

4.2 Primitive Transport Forms (Normative)

The following primitive forms are permitted. Each EY28 instance MUST declare which are used
in TransportDecl.

T1: Operator Pushforward

Given A1 in regime 1:
A2 := TA1S.

This is the primary operator-transport form.

Domain rule. If A1 is only defined on a subspace, the transport MUST include explicit
projectors or domain declarations. Otherwise: FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH.

T2: Operator Pullback

Given an operator/observable g2 in regime 2:

g1 := Sg2T.

Used when constraints or observables are defined in the target regime but need evaluation in the
source regime.

700



T3: State Transport (Density/State Object)

Given ρ1 in regime 1:
ρ2 := Tρ1S.

Special case where positivity/trace predicates may be asserted (P5).

T4: Constraint Transport (Predicate Carryover)

Constraints are transported by re-instantiation:

Comm(A1, B1) ⇝ Comm(A2, B2), A2 = TA1S, B2 = TB1S,

and then checked in regime 2 via an EY27 instance bound to regime 2 NumericModel/Truncation.

Rule. Constraints are never “transported by narrative”. They are transported by transported
objects + re-check routines.

4.3 Baseline Routine Set

EY28 defines baseline deterministic routines RoutineID ∈ RINTW
0 .

Routine INTW-R0: Direct Pushforward (Explicit T, S)

Inputs. Canonical encodings or hashes for T, S,A1.

Steps.
1. Canonicalize T, S,A1 under declared NumericModelLink rules.
2. Compute M := TA1 with fixed MulOrder/ReduceOrder.
3. Compute A2 := MS.
4. Canonicalize A2 at declared CanonPoints.
5. Commit transcript: hashes of T, S,A1, A2 and intermediate rules.

Outputs. Transported operator A2 (or its commitment), and transcript commitments.

Routine INTW-R1: Pullback (Explicit T, S)

Analogous to INTW-R0 but computes g1 := Sg2T .

Routine INTW-R2: Adjoint Back-Map Construction

If BackMapType is † and S not explicitly provided:

S := T †

computed deterministically:
• conjugate + transpose in a fixed order,

701



• canonicalize result,
• commit S by hash.

Routine INTW-R3: Inverse Back-Map Construction (Finite)

If BackMapType is (−1) and S not explicitly provided:

S := T−1

computed deterministically by a declared algorithm, baseline:
• LU decomposition with fixed pivot policy and tie-breaks,
• deterministic rounding/canonicalization at fixed points,
• reject if determinant test fails (within tolerance).

Failure. FAIL_NONINVERTIBLE if inversion fails deterministically.

Routine INTW-R4: Pseudo-Inverse Back-Map Construction (GEN)

If BackMapType is +:
S := T+

baseline algorithm: truncated SVD.
1. Compute SVD with fixed ordering conventions for singular vectors.
2. Apply a fixed singular-value threshold policy: σi < τ ⇒ σ−1

i = 0, with τ on a declared grid.
3. Recompose S deterministically and canonicalize.

Rule. All thresholds and tie-breaks MUST be declared. Otherwise: FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

Routine INTW-R5: Preservation Check Harness

A generic harness that evaluates PreserveSet predicates. It consumes:
• test sets V / F (committed by hash or seed),
• tolerances (explicit constants or grids),
• and the declared predicate list.

It outputs:
PreserveReport := {(Pred,Result,Value)}Pred∈PreserveSet

committed by hash.

4.4 INTW-0 Reference Profile (Baseline)

INTW-0 is the conservative baseline profile for EY28, analogous to FLOQ-0 and COMM-0.

702



INTW-0 Fixes

INTW-0 fixes:
• SemClass ∈ {UNIT, ISO} only,
• BackMapType = † (so S = T †),
• AlignPolicy = same-N (single truncation level N0),
• pushforward and pullback allowed; constraints transported only by re-check (T4),
• preservation predicates allowed: P1, P2, P3 (optional), P6 (only if explicitly re-checked via

EY27),
• pseudo-inverses and projected domains forbidden in baseline.

Rule. INTW-0 forbids GEN and PART semantics. If an artifact needs pseudo-inverses,
projectors, or multi-N alignment, it must declare a non-baseline profile.

4.5 Deterministic Failure Codes (Routine Layer)

At minimum:
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_NONINVERTIBLE
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH
• FAIL_PRESERVATION

4.6 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined primitive transport forms (pushforward, pullback, state transport, constraint
transport by re-check), introduced baseline deterministic routines (INTW-R0..R5) for computing
transported objects and back-maps, and defined the conservative INTW-0 reference profile:
unitary/isometric transport with adjoint back-map, same truncation alignment, and limited
preservation claims.
Chapter 5 next specifies certificate payload and verifier checks for EY28: how transported objects
and preservation reports are committed, how back-maps are validated, and how interop claims
