5 Certificate and Verifier: Transport Replay and Preservation
Acceptance

5.1 Purpose

EY28 is often used as the justification layer for “this workflow in regime 2 corresponds to that
workflow in regime 1”. Therefore, EY28 must publish more than a map: it must publish replayable

703



commitments for:
• the regime declarations,
• the maps T and S (or deterministic construction rules),
• the transported objects (when published),
• and the preservation predicate results used to support interop claims.

This chapter specifies:
• the certificate payload πINTW,
• deterministic verifier checks for acceptance,
• transcript commitments for transport computations,
• and required failure codes.

5.2 Certificate Object πINTW

Rule. An EY28 publication MUST include a certificate πINTW in canonical certificate encoding
(EY22-CCE).

Header (required)

• artifact type: INTW

• artifact symbol: T1→2

• RegimeID1, RegimeID2

• SemClass, BackMapType, AlignPolicy
• Version
• Certificate schema identifier (EY22-CCE)

SpecID (required)

The full SpecID tuple MUST be embedded:

SpecIDEY28 := (INTW, RegimeSpec1, RegimeSpec2, MapSpec(T ), MapSpec(S), TransportDecl, NumericModelLink, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Committed Inputs (required)

πINTW MUST commit to:
• RegimeSpec1, RegimeSpec2 (including Trunc and NumericModels),
• MapSpec(T ) and its content: inline encoding or hash-commitment or construction recipe +

inputs,
• MapSpec(S) and its content: explicit or derived by declared routine,
• TransportDecl fields (SemClass, BackMapType, PushPullForms, AlignPolicy, PreserveSet),
• NumericModelLink (NMPolicy and any coercion routines),

704



• all tolerances and test sets used by preservation predicates (explicit, hashed, or deterministic
seed).

Committed Outputs (required)

πINTW MUST commit to:
• a Transport Transcript Commitment Txintw,
• a Preservation Report Commitment Txpres covering all predicates in PreserveSet,
• transported objects if published as outputs (e.g. A2, ρ2) or their hashes,
• deterministic failure code if evaluation fails.

Transport Transcript (minimum contents)

At minimum, the transcript commitment MUST bind:
• hashes of T and S (or construction recipes + input hashes),
• hashes of the input objects transported (if any are part of the claim),
• declared routine IDs used (INTW-R0..R5 or committed equivalents),
• canonicalization points and multiplication/reduction order settings,
• truncation alignment decisions (including CrossNPolicy results if multi-N).

Preservation Report (minimum contents)

A preservation report must include a list:
PreserveReport := {(PredID,Result,Value,Tol)}

for each predicate in PreserveSet, with deterministic serialization and hashing.

Rule. Preservation predicates not listed in PreserveSet MUST NOT appear in the report as
“implied”. If they appear, reject as malformed.

5.3 Verifier Contract

A verifier consumes πINTW and returns:
{ACCEPT,REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗}.

Acceptance meaning. ACCEPT means: the transport artifact is well-formed, replayable,
and the declared preservation predicates (if any) hold under the declared routines. It does not
mean the regimes are “the same” or that any undeclared property is preserved.

5.4 Required Verifier Checks (Normative)

V1: Structural Validity (EY22-CCE)

Parse canonical certificate encoding and confirm required fields exist. Failure: REJECT_MALFORMED.

705



V2: SpecID Completeness and Consistency

Confirm:
• ArtifactType=INTW,
• both RegimeSpecs present,
• MapSpecs for T and S present,
• TransportDecl present (SemClass, BackMapType, AlignPolicy, PreserveSet),
• NumericModelLink present.

Failure: REJECT_SPECID_MISSING, REJECT_SEMCLASS_MISSING, RE-
JECT_BACKMAP_MISSING.

V3: Commitment Integrity

Verify all hash-committed objects resolve and match:
• T content or construction recipe,
• S content or construction recipe,
• test sets V/F and tolerances,
• any transported objects that are part of the claim.

Failure: FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH, REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT.

V4: NumericModel Linking Rules

Enforce NMPolicy:
• must-match: check equality of NumericModels,
• coerce: replay coercion routine deterministically,
• separate: enforce declared cross-check procedure.

Failure: FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH, FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

V5: Truncation Alignment

Enforce AlignPolicy:
• same-N : confirm N1 = N2 = N0,
• mapped-N : recompute N2 = f(N1),
• multi-N : apply CrossNPolicy and bind decisions,
• projected: validate projectors and domain declarations.

Failure: FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH, FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID.

706



V6: Back-Map Construction/Validation

If S is derived:
• adjoint: replay INTW-R2,
• inverse: replay INTW-R3,
• pseudo-inverse: replay INTW-R4.

Then validate required identities within tolerance based on SemClass:
• UNIT: TS ≈ I2 and ST ≈ I1,
• ISO: ST ≈ I1,
• PART: identities only on declared domains,
• GEN: pseudo-inverse conditions per routine spec.

Failure: FAIL_NONINVERTIBLE, FAIL_PRESERVATION, FAIL_NONDETERMINISM.

V7: Transport Replay (if objects are part of the claim)

If the certificate includes transported objects (or hashes), the verifier MUST replay transport:
• pushforward/pullback forms as declared,
• INTW-R0/INTW-R1 (or committed equivalents),
• canonicalization points and ordering rules.

Failure: FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH, FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

V8: Preservation Predicate Checks

For each predicate in PreserveSet, run the declared predicate routine (INTW-R5 harness) on
committed test sets and tolerances, and compare to the published Preservation Report. Failure:
FAIL_PRESERVATION, FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

V9: Interop Claim Consistency

If Interop claims composition with other artifacts:
• verify that referenced artifacts (by hash/SpecID) exist and match,
• verify that preservation claims listed are a subset of PreserveSet,
• for commutation preservation, verify that the workflow includes an EY27 re-check in regime

2.
Failure: FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE, FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED.

5.5 Acceptance Rule

Rule. A verifier returns ACCEPT iff:
• V1–V6 pass,

707



• any transported objects that are part of the claim replay deterministically,

• preservation report matches replay checks for all predicates in PreserveSet,

• transcript commitments match.
If any preservation predicate fails, the artifact may still be well-formed but must return
FAIL_PRESERVATION (not ACCEPT).

5.6 Required Failure Codes

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED

• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING

• REJECT_SEMCLASS_MISSING

• REJECT_BACKMAP_MISSING

• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT

• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH

• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH

• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH

• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID

• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM

• FAIL_NONINVERTIBLE

• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH

• FAIL_PRESERVATION

• FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE

• FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED

• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH

5.7 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the EY28 certificate πINTW and deterministic verifier checks: structural
validity, SpecID completeness, commitment integrity, NumericModel linking, truncation align-
ment, back-map construction/validation, transport replay, preservation predicate verification,
and interop claim consistency. It also fixed acceptance rules and required failure codes, making
EY28 a replayable transport artifact.
Chapter 7 next provides interoperability declarations (mini) for EY28: how transport composes
with EY23–EY30, how compatibility matrices should mark transported workflows, and how
interop certificates bind regime bridges deterministically.

708



6 Interop Declarations (Mini): Regime Bridges as Composable
Contracts

6.1 Purpose

EY28 exists so that workflows can move between regimes without informal interpretation. This
chapter instantiates EY22 interoperability rules for regime transport:

• how EY28 is referenced by other artifacts (and vice versa),
• what it means for a composition to be “transport-compatible”,
• how to write mini compatibility predicates for typical pairings (EY23–EY30),
• and what interop certificates must bind when a result depends on a regime bridge.

Rule. If a published claim depends on applying an artifact in regime 2 to an object transported
from regime 1 (or vice versa), the publication MUST include an interop certificate πinterop
referencing EY28 πINTW.

6.2 Interop Component Fields (Standard)

Any artifact that composes with EY28 MUST include an interop entry:

Interop ∋ (INTW-Ref, InteropRole, FormsUsed, PreserveClaims, Scope, CompatPredicates).

Required fields.
• INTW-Ref: hash/SpecID reference to πINTW (or SpecID hash) and RegimeIDs.
• InteropRole: one of source-bridge, target-bridge, two-way, constraint-bridge.
• FormsUsed: pushforward/pullback/state/constraint transport forms actually used.
• PreserveClaims: subset of PreserveSet asserted for this composition.
• Scope: which objects are transported (e.g. H, V , L, step set, summaries).
• CompatPredicates: identifiers of the compatibility predicates used (defined below).

Rule. PreserveClaims MUST be a subset of EY28 PreserveSet. Otherwise: FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE.

6.3 Compatibility Predicates (EY28 Mini Set)

EY28 standardizes a minimal predicate set for common interop reasoning.

INTW-C0: SpecID/Certificate Binding

INTW-C0 := (EIF INTW-Ref matches a valid πINTW and RegimeIDs align).

INTW-C1: Form Consistency

INTW-C1 := (EIF the composition uses only forms declared in TransportDecl.PushPullForms).

709



INTW-C2: NumericModel/Truncation Alignment

INTW-C2 := (EIF NMPolicy and AlignPolicy requirements are satisfied for the composed workflow).

INTW-C3: Preservation Claims Supported

INTW-C3 := (EIF each asserted preserve claim has a corresponding PASS entry in PreserveReport).

INTW-C4: Object Commitment Closure

INTW-C4 := (EIF all transported objects used downstream are committed by hash or replayable by routine transcripts).

INTW-C5: Constraint Transport Is Re-Checked

For constraint transport (e.g. commutation):

INTW-C5 := (EIF constraints are transported by transporting objects and re-checking via the target predicate routine).

Rule. Any workflow asserting preservation of an EY27 commutation predicate MUST satisfy
INTW-C5 and MUST cite the target-regime EY27 PredID.

6.4 EY28 Pairwise Interop: Standard Mini Declarations

This section lists the intended composition semantics with EY23–EY30. These are templates;
real workflows must cite predicate IDs.

INTW ↔ CSF (EY23): Transported Filtering

Typical workflow. Transport H1 7→ H2, then apply F⋆(H2) in regime 2.

Compatibility template. Mark OK∗ if:

INTW-C0 ∧ INTW-C1 ∧ INTW-C2 ∧ INTW-C4

and if any spectral-class preservation is claimed, require:

INTW-C3 with P4 present in PreserveSet.

INTW ↔ VPO (EY24): Transported Validity Penalties

Typical workflow. Transport a validity operator V1 7→ V2 or transport constraint object K
used to build V .

Compatibility template. OK∗ if:

INTW-C0 ∧ INTW-C2 ∧ INTW-C4

and if positivity/trace preservation is claimed for state evolution under validity, require P5 with
PASS.

710



INTW ↔ LIOUV (EY25): Transported Generators and Evolutions

Two patterns are allowed:

Pattern A (generator transport). Transport the generator (Hamiltonian/Liouvillian) and
evolve in regime 2.

Pattern B (trajectory transport). Evolve in regime 1 and transport snapshots/states to
regime 2.

Compatibility template. OK∗ if:

INTW-C0 ∧ INTW-C2 ∧ INTW-C4

plus explicit declaration of which pattern is used. If invariants are claimed preserved, require
INTW-C3 with those predicates present.

INTW ↔ FLOQ (EY26): Transported Step Sets and Tokens

Typical workflow. Transport step operators Uj,1 7→ Uj,2 and build/verify a token in regime 2.

Compatibility template. OK∗ if:

INTW-C0 ∧ INTW-C1 ∧ INTW-C2 ∧ INTW-C4

and if the token claims to preserve a commutation symmetry, require INTW-C5 and a target-
regime EY27 PredID.

INTW ↔ COMM (EY27): Transported Commutation Constraints

Canonical rule. Commutation constraints are transported by transporting the objects and
re-checking:

A2 = TA1S, B2 = TB1S, Comm(A2, B2) checked via EY27 in regime 2.

Compatibility template. OK∗ iff INTW-C5 holds and NumericModel/Truncation alignment
is satisfied.

INTW ↔ CGR (EY29): Transport as Reduction

Transport can be a reduction (when N2 < N1 or when PART semantics apply). In that case, the
workflow MUST declare whether EY28 is effectively performing coarse-grain and must use EY29
invariants/tolerances.

Compatibility template. OK∗ if:

INTW-C0 ∧ INTW-C2 ∧ INTW-C4

and any reduction-preservation claim requires explicit EY29 certificates.

711



INTW ↔ KOOP (EY30): Export Across Representations

Koopman export often changes representation (state-space to observable-space). EY28 provides
the bridge typing, but preservation claims must be explicit (P3/P4/P5 depending on semantics).

Compatibility template. OK∗ if INTW-C0..C4 hold and the workflow declares the export
semantics mapping.

6.5 Interop Certificates for Regime-Bridged Workflows

Whenever a claim depends on an EY28 bridge, the workflow SHOULD publish an interop
certificate:
πinterop := (SpecIDs of all artifacts, INTW-Ref, FormsUsed, Scope, PreserveClaims, CompatPredicates, TranscriptRefs).

Rule. If the outcome is published as an artifact-derived claim (e.g. spectral bucket assignment,
regime bridge, Koopman invariant), an interop certificate MUST be provided if the claim depends
on cross-regime composition.

6.6 Deterministic Interop Failure Codes

At minimum:
• FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE
• FAIL_NUMERICMODEL_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_PRESERVATION
• FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH

6.7 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the EY28 interoperability mini-language: how INTW references appear in
other artifacts’ Interop components, a minimal set of compatibility predicates (INTW-C0..C5),
and standard pairwise interop templates for composing EY28 with EY23–EY30. It also defined
interop certificates for regime-bridged workflows and required deterministic failure codes.
Chapter ?? next provides an INTW-0 reference SpecID template, fixes the publication boundary
and non-claims for EY28, and closes the artifact in a QFC-consistent way.

8 Worked Examples (Non-Normative): Regime Bridges in Vol.
No. IV

8.1 Purpose

This chapter is non-normative. It illustrates typical EY28 usage patterns:
• transporting a Hamiltonian and applying a canonical spectral filter (EY23),
• transporting a validity penalty (EY24) and preserving positivity claims,
• bridging a Liouvillian evolution (EY25) by generator-transport vs trajectory-transport,
• transporting a program token step set (EY26),
• transporting commutation constraints (EY27) by re-check,
• and bridging into observable space for Koopman export (EY30).

716



Reminder. Examples are schematic. They become valid only when all objects are canonically
encoded or hash-committed, and NumericModel/Truncation alignment is explicit.

8.2 Example 1: Transport H1 and Filter in Regime 2 (EY23)

Goal. Compute a filtered operator in regime 2:

H2 := TH1S, H̃2 := F⋆(H2).

Artifact chain.
• EY28 publishes T, S and commits H2 (or commits the transcript needed to replay it).
• EY23 in regime 2 takes H2 as input and publishes SpecIDEY23 with its own NumericModel.
• Interop certificate binds: INTW-Ref, CSF-Ref, the exact forms used (pushforward then

filter), and the preserved predicates needed for the claim (often none beyond transport
replay).

Common pitfall. Claiming “spectral class preserved” without P4 in PreserveSet and a PASS
entry in PreserveReport.

8.3 Example 2: Transport a Validity Penalty V (EY24)

Goal. Move a validity operator to regime 2:

V2 := TV1S,

so a verifier can enforce the same validity constraints in regime 2.

If positivity of states is claimed. If the workflow asserts that mapping preserves positivity
of a transported density:

ρ2 := Tρ1S ⪰ 0,
then EY28 must include P5 in PreserveSet with deterministic positivity test rules (eigenvalue
threshold grid).

Common pitfall. Assuming positivity is preserved just because S = T †. That is only
guaranteed if the map is truly unitary/isometric under the declared truncation and numeric
policy—and even then, Vol. No. IV requires explicit declaration and check.

8.4 Example 3: Liouvillian Bridge (EY25) — Two Patterns

Pattern A: Generator Transport

Goal. Transport the generator L1 to L2 and evolve in regime 2:

L2 := TL1S, ρ2(t) = etL2ρ2(0).

This requires explicit declaration of how superoperators are transported and represented (Map-
Type may be factored/constructed).

717



Pattern B: Trajectory Transport

Goal. Evolve in regime 1 and transport snapshots:

ρ2(tk) := Tρ1(tk)S,

for a declared checkpoint set {tk}.

Common pitfall. Mixing the two patterns without declaring it; verifiers cannot know whether
generator transport or trajectory transport was used.

8.5 Example 4: Token Step-Set Transport (EY26)

Goal. Build a token in regime 2 from steps defined in regime 1:

∏m
Uj,2 := TUj,1S, UF,2 := Uj,2.

j=1

Interop binding. Interop must declare:
• scope: “step operators” {Uj},
• forms: pushforward,
• and whether token verification occurs per-step or per-period (CommCheckScope if symmetry

is involved).

8.6 Example 5: Transporting an EY27 Constraint (Re-check in Regime 2)

Goal. Given a commutation claim in regime 1:

Comm(A1, B1) = TRUE,

transport the objects and re-check in regime 2:

A2 := TA1S, B2 := TB1S, Comm(A2, B2) = TRUE.

Required publication.
• EY28 transcript commitments for A2, B2 or replay construction.
• A target-regime EY27 instance (PredID2) that defines commutation under regime-2 Nu-

mericModel/Trunc.
• Interop certificate that includes INTW-C5 and cites both PredID1 and PredID2 where

relevant.

Common pitfall. Claiming that commutation is preserved under transport without re-check.
Vol. No. IV forbids this as a default.

718



8.7 Example 6: Bridge Into Observable Space (Koopman Export, EY30)

Goal. Move from a state/operator regime into an observable regime where a Koopman operator
acts:

g1 ←−
pu−ll−b−ac−k− g2, K2(g2) = g2 ◦ Φ,

and bind the relationship between state evolution and observable evolution.

What must be declared.
• whether the bridge is pullback-only,
• how observables are represented (RegimeSpec2.SpaceType),
• what preservation predicates are meaningful (often P3 and possibly P4),
• and which claims are non-claims (e.g. state positivity may not translate to observable

space).

8.8 Chapter Summary

This non-normative chapter illustrated EY28 in common Vol. No. IV workflows: transporting
Hamiltonians for filtering (EY23), transporting validity penalties and positivity claims (EY24),
bridging Liouvillian evolution by generator vs trajectory transport (EY25), transporting token
step sets (EY26), transporting commutation constraints via object transport + re-check (EY27),
and bridging into observable space for Koopman export (EY30).

Next. Proceed to EY29: Coarse-Grain Reducer R, which makes explicit how reductions
weaken or preserve invariants and how bucketed, verifier-friendly summaries are produced from
high-resolution operator artifacts.

719



Chapter 29

EY29: Coarse-Grain Reducer R
Canonical Operator Artifacts for QFC

Enter Yourname

Abstract
This whitepaper defines the Coarse-Grain Reducer R, a canonical arti-
fact that reduces high-resolution operator objects into verifier-friendly
summaries and lower-resolution representations while preserving (or ex-
plicitly weakening) declared invariants. EY29 standardizes reduction
semantics: which degrees of freedom are eliminated, how truncation levels
are mapped, what invariants are preserved, and how loss is measured
and certified.

R is the bridge from spectral probing to machine-checkable buckets: it converts outputs of
canonical spectral filters (EY23), validity penalties (EY24), audit-native evolutions (EY25), and
regime transport (EY28) into reduced operators, reduced certificates, and coarse observables
usable for classification, compatibility matrices, and Koopman export (EY30). Every reduction
claim in Vol. No. IV must be replayable under a declared NumericModel, with deterministic
failure codes and interop certificates.

1 Motivation and Scope: From High-Resolution Operators to
Verifier-Friendly Summaries

1.1 Motivation: Why Coarse-Grain Must Be a First-Class Artifact

Vol. No. IV introduces operator artifacts intended to be composed and verified: filters (EY23),
validity penalties (EY24), audit-native evolution (EY25), tokens (EY26), commutation constraints
(EY27), and regime bridges (EY28). In practice, however, these objects are often too large or
too detailed to:

• transmit widely,
• replay quickly by many verifiers,
• compare across runs and machines,
• or use as stable classification labels for registries and compatibility matrices.

Therefore, workflows require reduction: turning a detailed operator object into a smaller repre-
sentation or summary. But reduction is also the primary place where meaning gets smuggled:

• hidden thresholds,
• unlogged truncations,
• heuristic feature extraction,



• and “it looks the same” reasoning.
EY29 exists to prevent that. It makes coarse-graining an auditable artifact with a SpecID,
deterministic routines, and certificates.

1.2 What EY29 Defines

EY29 defines:
• a canonical reducer R that maps detailed objects to reduced objects,
• reduction semantics classes (projection, aggregation, bucketing, sketching),
• truncation mapping policies (how N changes),
• invariant preservation/weakening rules (what remains true, what becomes approximate,

what is discarded),
• loss metrics that are explicitly computed and committed,
• a certificate/verifier contract for deterministic replay,
• interop declarations with other artifacts (especially EY23, EY24, EY28, EY30).

1.3 Scope

In-scope.
• Reduction of operators: A 7→ Ã = R(A).
• Reduction of state objects and summaries (when explicitly declared).
• Reduction of certificates: producing reduced certificates or summary commitments.
• Declaring and checking which invariants are preserved vs weakened.

Out-of-scope.
• “Black-box compression” without deterministic reconstruction rules.
• Learned embeddings without committed parameters and deterministic replay.
• Claims of infinite-dimensional equivalence inferred solely from reduced summaries.

1.4 Intuition: Reduction as a Typed Map with a Loss Budget

A reducer is not merely a function; it is a typed map with declared semantics:
R : X → X̃ ,

where X is an object class (operators, states, spectra, transcripts) and X̃ is a smaller class
intended for verifier-friendly handling.
Reduction must bind:

• what is removed (degrees of freedom),
• what is kept (invariants and summaries),
• how much is lost (loss metrics),
• how to reproduce it (deterministic routines).

721



1.5 Why EY29 Is Central to “Buckets” and Registries

Vol. No. IV intends to support a registry and compatibility matrix (EY22): to compare artifacts
across runs and to classify them into stable spectral classes.
But classification requires stable signatures. High-resolution objects are too sensitive to:

• truncation edges,
• floating point drift,
• minor parameter changes,
• ordering differences.

A reducer supplies a canonical, auditable signature layer :
Sig(A) := Enc(R(A)),

where Enc is canonical encoding/hashing bound to NumericModel.

Rule. If a workflow uses a reduced signature as a registry key, it MUST cite EY29 SpecID and
include loss metrics and tolerance policies so the key is meaningful and replayable.

1.6 Design Goals (Normative)

G1: Deterministic Reduction

Given the same inputs, SpecID, truncation policy, and NumericModel, every verifier MUST
compute the same reduced object.

G2: Explicit Loss Accounting

Every reduction MUST produce explicit loss metrics and commit them in the certificate. If a
loss metric is “not applicable”, it must be explicitly null.

G3: Declared Invariant Preservation

Invariants are preserved only if explicitly declared and checked. Otherwise, no preservation claim
is implied.

G4: Compatibility with Vol. No. IV Workflows

EY29 must compose with:
• EY23 filters (reducing filtered outputs),
• EY24 penalties (reducing validity objects or their summaries),
• EY25 evolutions (reducing snapshots/summary observables),
• EY26 tokens (reducing step sets or token-derived summaries),
• EY27 constraints (reducing objects while tracking commutation loss),
• EY28 bridges (treating transport as reduction when N shrinks),
• EY30 Koopman export (reducing to observable-space summaries).

722



1.7 Chapter Summary

This chapter motivated EY29: coarse-graining is required for verifier-friendly operation, but
it is also the primary place where meaning is smuggled. EY29 makes reduction an auditable

declared preservation, and composability across Vol. No. IV.

2 Motivation and Scope: From High-Resolution Operators to
Verifier-Friendly Summaries

2.1 Motivation: Why Coarse-Grain Must Be a First-Class Artifact

Vol. No. IV introduces operator artifacts intended to be composed and verified: filters (EY23),
validity penalties (EY24), audit-native evolution (EY25), tokens (EY26), commutation constraints
(EY27), and regime bridges (EY28). In practice, however, these objects are often too large or
too detailed to:

• transmit widely,
• replay quickly by many verifiers,
• compare across runs and machines,
• or use as stable classification labels for registries and compatibility matrices.

Therefore, workflows require reduction: turning a detailed operator object into a smaller repre-
sentation or summary. But reduction is also the primary place where meaning gets smuggled:

• hidden thresholds,
• unlogged truncations,
• heuristic feature extraction,
• and “it looks the same” reasoning.

EY29 exists to prevent that. It makes coarse-graining an auditable artifact with a SpecID,
deterministic routines, and certificates.

2.2 What EY29 Defines

EY29 defines:
• a canonical reducer R that maps detailed objects to reduced objects,
• reduction semantics classes (projection, aggregation, bucketing, sketching),
• truncation mapping policies (how N changes),
• invariant preservation/weakening rules (what remains true, what becomes approximate,

what is discarded),
• loss metrics that are explicitly computed and committed,

723



• a certificate/verifier contract for deterministic replay,
• interop declarations with other artifacts (especially EY23, EY24, EY28, EY30).

2.3 Scope

In-scope.
• Reduction of operators: A 7→ Ã = R(A).
• Reduction of state objects and summaries (when explicitly declared).
• Reduction of certificates: producing reduced certificates or summary commitments.
• Declaring and checking which invariants are preserved vs weakened.

Out-of-scope.
• “Black-box compression” without deterministic reconstruction rules.
• Learned embeddings without committed parameters and deterministic replay.
• Claims of infinite-dimensional equivalence inferred solely from reduced summaries.

2.4 Intuition: Reduction as a Typed Map with a Loss Budget

A reducer is not merely a function; it is a typed map with declared semantics:

• how to reproduce it (deterministic routines).

3 Artifact Structure and SpecID Schema

3.1 Purpose

Chapters 2–?? motivated reduction and defined semantics classes, truncation mapping policies,
and invariant vocabulary. This chapter defines EY29 as an auditable artifact with a precise
SpecID schema:

• how the reducer R is represented (explicit, factored, constructed),
• how partitions/seeds/thresholds/classifiers are committed,
• how invariants and loss metrics are bound to check routines,
• and what transcript/certificate payload is required for deterministic replay.

3.2 Reducer as a Typed Object

EY29 treats a reducer as a typed map:

R : X → X̃ ,

where X is an input object class and X̃ is the reduced object class.

InputType and OutputType

Each EY29 instance MUST declare:

InputType ∈ {OP,STATE,CERT, SUMMARY}, OutputType ∈ {OP,STATE,CERT, SUMMARY,BUCKET}.

Rule. If OutputType = BUCKET, the artifact MUST publish bucket label rules and classifier
commitments (RedClass=BUCK).

3.3 ReducerSpec

EY29 standardizes a reducer declaration object:

ReducerSpec := (RedClass, NMap, ReducerCore, InvPolicy, LossSpec).

ReducerCore

ReducerCore encodes the mechanism of reduction and is class-dependent.

Class PROJ (R1).

ReducerCorePROJ := (ProjType, ProjEncoding, ProjRoutine, ProjChecks)

where P is explicit or constructed deterministically, and projector checks include idempotence/self-
adjointness tolerances.

726



Class AGG (R2).

ReducerCoreAGG := (PartitionSpec, Φ, OrderSpec)

where PartitionSpec binds the block partition and Φ binds the aggregation functional and its
deterministic evaluation order.

Class BUCK (R3).

ReducerCoreBUCK := (ClassifierSpec, SummarySpec, CrossNPolicy)

where ClassifierSpec commits bucket rules and SummarySpec commits a bounded-size summary
encoding.

Class SKETCH (R4).

ReducerCoreSKETCH := (PRNGSpec, Seed, SketchGen, SketchForm)

where SketchGen deterministically generates the sketch operator or sketch vector transform.

Class THR (R5).

ReducerCoreTHR := (τ, ThreshGrid, TieBreak, ScanOrder)

where thresholds are explicit or quantized grids, and ScanOrder fixes entry iteration deterministi-
cally.

Rule (null discipline). Any ReducerCore field that is not used MUST appear as null
(explicit). Omission is not allowed.

3.4 Invariant Policy Binding

InvPolicy is the contract for what the reduction preserves/weakens/discards.

Schema.
InvPolicy := {(InvName, Status, TolSpec, CheckRoutineID)}.

Rule. If Status = preserved or weakened, then TolSpec and CheckRoutineID MUST be
present. If Status = discarded, both MUST be null.

3.5 LossSpec

LossSpec binds loss metrics to explicit deterministic routines.

Schema.
LossSpec := {(LossName, ValueType, TolSpec, RoutineID)}.

Rule. At least one loss metric MUST be declared (Chapter ??). If a loss metric is not applicable,
it must be explicitly null and justified by RedClass.

727



3.6 NumericModel and Truncation Binding

EY29 is only meaningful under declared numeric/truncation semantics.

TruncSpec

TruncSpec := (Basis, CutRule, BoundaryRule, Nin, Nout, CrossNPolicy).

Rule. If NMap is same-N , then Nin = Nout. If NMap is shrink-N , the mapping rule and
rounding MUST be declared.

NumericModel

NumericModel MUST bind:
• arithmetic type (float/fixed/exact),

• rounding/precision,

• deterministic matmul rules (order and accumulation),

• canonicalization rules and points.

3.7 TranscriptSpec and Commitments

Reduction must be replayable. Therefore, transcript commitments MUST bind:
• reducer core parameters (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold),

• truncation mapping decisions (especially for multi-N),

• reduced output object Ã (or its hash),

• all invariant check results and loss metric values,

• deterministic scan orders and tie-breaks used.

Rule. If the reduced output is used as a registry key or bucket label, the transcript MUST
bind enough data to recompute it exactly.

3.8 SpecID for EY29

ArtifactType. For EY29:
ArtifactType = CGR.

SpecID components (EY29 binding). The full SpecID tuple is:

SpecIDEY29 := (CGR, InputType, OutputType, ReducerSpec, TruncSpec, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

728



Interop (Mini)

Interop binds intended compositions:
• references to upstream artifacts whose outputs are reduced (EY23/EY24/EY25/EY26/EY28/EY27),
• invariant obligations inherited from those artifacts (e.g. validity, commutation),
• and compatibility predicates for workflows.

Rule. If EY29 reduces an object whose meaning depends on EY27 or EY24, InvPolicy MUST
include I6 Commutation and/or I7 Validity as preserved/weakened (not discarded), unless
the workflow explicitly declares it does not depend on those invariants.

3.9 Deterministic Failure Codes (Schema Layer)

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_REDCLASS_MISSING
• REJECT_NMAP_MISSING
• REJECT_INVPOLICY_MISSING
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH
• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED
• FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED

3.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the EY29 artifact schema: InputType/OutputType, a ReducerSpec binding
reduction class, truncation mapping, reducer core parameters, invariant policy, and loss specifica-
tion; plus truncation and NumericModel binding, transcript commitments, and an interop mini
layer. It fixed the full SpecID tuple for EY29 and required schema-layer failure codes.
Chapter 4 next defines baseline deterministic routines (CGR-0) for each reduction class and
specifies how reducers compute reduced outputs, loss metrics, and invariant checks in a verifier-
replayable way.

4 Baseline Deterministic Routines (CGR-0)

4.1 Purpose

A reducer is only useful if verifiers can replay it. This chapter defines:

729



• a baseline routine set for computing reduced objects Ã = R(A),
• deterministic harnesses for invariant checks and loss metrics,
• and a conservative reference profile CGR-0.

Rule. Every EY29 instance MUST declare the RoutineID used for reduction, invariant checks,
and loss metrics (either from this baseline set or via a committed equivalent). Hidden routines
are forbidden.

4.2 Routine Set Overview

EY29 defines baseline routines RoutineID ∈ RCGR
0 :

• CGR-R0: canonical input preparation and validation
• CGR-R1: PROJ reduction
• CGR-R2: AGG reduction
• CGR-R3: BUCK reduction
• CGR-R4: SKETCH reduction
• CGR-R5: THR reduction
• CGR-R6: invariant check harness
• CGR-R7: loss metric harness
• CGR-R8: multi-N aggregation (CrossNPolicy harness)

4.3 CGR-R0: Canonical Input Preparation

Inputs. A (operator/state/cert/summary) with declared encoding, plus SpecID, TruncSpec,
NumericModel.

Steps.
1. Parse and validate InputType/encoding.
2. Canonicalize A under NumericModel (encoding normalization + declared canon points).
3. Validate domain/type constraints (e.g. square matrix for OP).
4. Commit input hash hA.

Failure. FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH if type constraints fail; REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
if encoding is not bound.

4.4 CGR-R1: PROJ Reduction (Projection/Restriction)

Inputs. Prepared A, projector P (explicit or constructed), projector checks/tolerances.

730



Steps.
1. Obtain P by inline encoding, hash resolution, or deterministic construction recipe.
2. Validate projector properties (deterministic):

∥P 2 − P∥F ≤ εP , ∥P − P †∥F ≤ εP .

3. Compute Ã := PAP with fixed MulOrder/ReduceOrder.
4. Canonicalize Ã.
5. Commit h and intermediate hashes as declared.

Ã

Failure. FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID if projector checks fail; FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
if routines are underspecified.

4.5 CGR-R2: AGG Reduction (Block Aggregation)

Inputs. Prepared A, PartitionSpec {Bi}, aggregation functional Φ, deterministic OrderSpec.

Steps.
1. Resolve PartitionSpec deterministically (explicit list, hash, or seed+generator).
2. For each output block pair (i, j) in deterministic scan order: compute the multiset {Apq}

for p ∈ Bi, q ∈ Bj , then compute Ãij := Φ(·) using a fixed reduction order.
3. Canonicalize Ã and commit hash.

Failure. FAIL_PARTITION_INVALID if blocks overlap/omit indices beyond declared
policy.

4.6 CGR-R3: BUCK Reduction (Bucket + Summary)

Inputs. Prepared A, ClassifierSpec, SummarySpec, truncation policy (single-N or multi-N).

Steps (single-N).
1. Compute a deterministic feature vector f(A) (must be defined in ClassifierSpec).
2. Evaluate deterministic classifier C to produce a discrete label:

BucketID := C(f(A)).

3. Compute bounded summary s(A) as in SummarySpec (e.g. top-k spectral stats, bounded
moments).

4. Output R(A) := (BucketID, s(A)) and commit by canonical encoding.

Steps (multi-N). For Nin = {N (1), . . . , N (K)}, repeat the above per N (k) and invoke CGR-R8
CrossNPolicy.

731



Failure. FAIL_CLASSIFIER_UNDEFINED if classifier rules are not fully committed.

4.7 CGR-R4: SKETCH Reduction (Deterministic Pseudorandom Sketch)

Inputs. Prepared A, PRNGSpec, Seed, SketchGen routine, SketchForm.

Steps.
1. Generate sketch operator/transform S deterministically from (PRNGSpec, Seed).
2. Compute sketch output (one of):

Ã := SAS† or ṽ := S · vec(A).

3. Canonicalize output and commit hash.

Failure. FAIL_NONDETERMINISM if PRNGSpec or generator is underspecified.

4.8 CGR-R5: THR Reduction (Thresholding/Sparsification)

Inputs. Prepared A, threshold τ (or grid), ScanOrder, TieBreak.

Steps.
1. Fix τ deterministically (explicit constant or quantized grid index).
2. For each entry in ScanOrder: apply threshold rule; on equality, apply TieBreak policy

deterministically.
3. Canonicalize Ã, commit hash, and record sparsity statistics.

Failure. FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED if the reduction does not compute ∥A− Ã∥ (unless
explicitly null and justified).

4.9 CGR-R6: Invariant Check Harness

Inputs. InvPolicy list, input A, reduced output Ã, and any referenced artifacts (EY27 PredID,
EY24 validity, etc.).

Steps. For each (InvName, Status,TolSpec,CheckRoutineID):
1. If Status=discarded: record null and continue.
2. Else run CheckRoutineID deterministically and record: (InvName,Result,Value,Tol).

Outputs. Invariant report committed by canonical encoding/hashing.

4.10 CGR-R7: Loss Metric Harness

Inputs. LossSpec list, A, Ã, truncation, NumericModel.

732



Steps. For each declared loss metric:
1. compute its value deterministically under declared norms/orders,
2. record the value and tolerance (if applicable),
3. commit the loss report.

Outputs. Loss report committed by canonical encoding/hashing.

4.11 CGR-R8: Multi-N CrossNPolicy Harness

Inputs. Per-N outputs {RN(k)(A)} and declared CrossNPolicy.

Steps.
1. Apply CrossNPolicy deterministically to aggregate: BucketID and/or summaries across N .
2. Record stabilization diagnostics (e.g. first k where label stabilizes) if declared.

Outputs. Aggregated reduced object and CrossN transcript commitments.

4.12 CGR-0 Reference Profile (Baseline)

CGR-0 is the conservative baseline profile for EY29.

CGR-0 Fixes

CGR-0 fixes:
• RedClass ∈ {PROJ,AGG,BUCK} only,
• NMap ∈ {same-N, shrink-N} (multi-N is non-baseline),
• no SKETCH unless explicitly seeded and committed (recommended non-baseline),
• no THR unless thresholds are fixed constants (recommended non-baseline),
• mandatory loss metrics: ∥A− Ã∥F for PROJ/AGG/THR; “margin/stability” for BUCK,
• invariant vocabulary must include I1 (Domain) and I8 (Replay), and any workflow-dependent

invariants (I6/I7) cannot be discarded.

Rule. If a reducer uses SKETCH or THR with a grid of thresholds, it MUST declare a
non-baseline profile and publish full determinism rules.

4.13 Routine-Layer Failure Codes

At minimum:
• FAIL_PROJECTOR_INVALID
• FAIL_PARTITION_INVALID
• FAIL_CLASSIFIER_UNDEFINED

733



• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM

• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH

• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH

• FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED

• FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED

4.14 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined baseline deterministic routines (CGR-R0..R8) for computing reduced objects
under each reduction class, evaluating invariant policies, computing loss metrics, and aggregating
across truncations with CrossNPolicy. It also defined the conservative CGR-0 reference profile:
limited reduction classes, restricted N -mapping, and mandatory loss/invariant accounting.
Chapter 6 next specifies certificate payload and verifier checks for EY29: how reduced outputs,
invariant reports, and loss reports are committed and replayed, and how reducers are accepted
or rejected deterministically.

5 Certificate and Verifier: Reduction Replay, Loss Accounting,
and Invariant Acceptance

5.1 Purpose

EY29 reductions are used as registry keys, bucket labels, and verifier-friendly summaries. There-
fore, a reducer must publish:

• the full reducer SpecID (including ReducerCore parameters),

• deterministic transcripts that allow replay,

• invariant check results (per InvPolicy),

• loss metrics (per LossSpec),

• and failure codes when reduction cannot be accepted.
This chapter specifies:

• the certificate payload πCGR,

• deterministic verifier checks for acceptance,

• transcript commitments for reduction computations,

• and required failure codes.

5.2 Certificate Object πCGR

Rule. An EY29 publication MUST include a certificate πCGR in canonical certificate encoding
(EY22-CCE).

734



Header (required)

• artifact type: CGR

• artifact symbol: R
• RedClass, NMap, InputType, OutputType
• Version
• Certificate schema identifier (EY22-CCE)

SpecID (required)

The full SpecID tuple MUST be embedded:

SpecIDEY29 := (CGR, InputType, OutputType, ReducerSpec, TruncSpec, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Committed Inputs (required)

πCGR MUST commit to:
• ReducerSpec including ReducerCore (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold),
• TruncSpec including Nin, Nout and any CrossNPolicy rules,
• NumericModel (including ordering/canonicalization),
• InvPolicy (names, statuses, tolerances, check routines),
• LossSpec (definitions, routines, tolerances or explicit null),
• any external referenced objects used by invariant checks (e.g. EY27 PredID, EY24 validity,

EY28 bridge transcripts),
• input object commitment hA (or a reference to the upstream artifact output hash).

Committed Outputs (required)

πCGR MUST commit to:
• reduced output object Ã (or its hash) and canonical encoding rule,
• reduction transcript commitment Txcgr,
• invariant report commitment Txinv,
• loss report commitment Txloss,
• deterministic failure code if reduction or checks fail.

5.3 Reduction Transcript (Minimum Contents)

The reduction transcript MUST bind enough information to replay:
• input hash hA and any upstream references (artifact IDs, output hashes),
• reducer core resolution (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold) and their hashes,
• truncation mapping decisions (including rounding/tie-breaks and CrossNPolicy outputs),

735



• deterministic scan orders (block order, entry order, reduction order),
• canonicalization points and rules,
• reduced output hash h (or hash of bucket+summary encoding).

Ã

Rule (registry-grade output). If Ã or BucketID is used as a registry key, πCGR MUST
include:

• a stable canonical encoding of the key material,
• and the exact CrossNPolicy (if any) that produced it.

5.4 Invariant Report (Required Structure)

An invariant report is the canonical serialization of:

InvReport := {(InvName,Status,Result,Value,Tol)}.

Rule. For Status = discarded, Result, Value, Tol MUST be null. For preserved/weakened
invariants, they MUST be non-null.

5.5 Loss Report (Required Structure)

A loss report is the canonical serialization of:

LossReport := {(LossName,Value,Tol)}.

Rule. If a loss metric is declared but not computed, Value MUST be null, and the verifier
must check that the SpecID justification exists. Otherwise: FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED.

5.6 Verifier Contract

A verifier consumes πCGR and returns:

{ACCEPT,REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗}.

Acceptance meaning. ACCEPT means: the reducer artifact is well-formed, replayable, the
reduced output matches replay, loss metrics are computed as declared, and invariants marked
preserved/weakened satisfy their check rules within tolerance. It does not imply any invariant
marked discarded, and it does not imply preservation beyond InvPolicy.

5.7 Required Verifier Checks (Normative)

V1: Structural Validity (EY22-CCE)

Parse canonical certificate encoding and confirm required fields exist. Failure: REJECT_MALFORMED.

736



V2: SpecID Completeness

Confirm:
• ArtifactType=CGR,
• InputType, OutputType,
• ReducerSpec (RedClass, NMap, ReducerCore, InvPolicy, LossSpec),
• TruncSpec, NumericModel,
• TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version.

Failure: REJECT_SPECID_MISSING, REJECT_REDCLASS_MISSING, RE-
JECT_NMAP_MISSING, REJECT_INVPOLICY_MISSING.

V3: Commitment Integrity

Verify all hash-committed objects resolve and match:
• reducer core components (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold),
• input commitment hA (or upstream output hash),
• any referenced external artifacts used by invariant checks (PredIDs, validity objects),
• transcript commitments.

Failure: FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH, REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT.

V4: Truncation and NMap Enforcement

Enforce NMap and TruncSpec:
• same-N : check Nin = Nout,
• shrink-N : recompute declared mapping and rounding,
• multi-N : verify lists and CrossNPolicy selection (if used).

Failure: FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

V5: Reduction Replay

Replay reduction deterministically:
• run CGR-R0 preparation,
• run the declared reduction routine for RedClass (CGR-R1..R5) and CGR-R8 if multi-N ,
• apply declared scan orders and canonicalization points.

Compare the replayed reduced output hash to published h (or bucket+summary encoding
Ã

hash). Failure: FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH, FAIL_NONDETERMINISM,
FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH.

737



V6: Loss Metric Replay

Replay all loss metrics in LossSpec via CGR-R7. Compare to published LossReport. Failure:
FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED, FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

V7: Invariant Check Replay

Replay all preserved/weakened invariants via CGR-R6, including any referenced EY27/EY24/EY28
routines. Compare to published InvReport. Failure: FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED,
FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE, FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

V8: Interop Claim Consistency

If Interop claims composition with other artifacts:
• verify referenced artifacts (by hash/SpecID) exist and match,
• verify that invariants required by those workflows are not marked discarded in InvPolicy,
• verify that BUCK outputs used as keys include CrossNPolicy and stability diagnostics if

declared.
Failure: FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE.

5.8 Acceptance Rule

Rule. A verifier returns ACCEPT iff:
• V1–V5 pass,
• LossReport matches replayed loss metrics for all declared metrics,
• InvReport matches replayed invariant checks for all preserved/weakened invariants,
• transcript commitments match.

If an invariant marked preserved fails, return FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED
(not ACCEPT).

5.9 Required Failure Codes

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_REDCLASS_MISSING
• REJECT_NMAP_MISSING
• REJECT_INVPOLICY_MISSING
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH

738



• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH
• FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED
• FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED
• FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE

5.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the EY29 certificate πCGR and deterministic verifier checks: SpecID
completeness, commitment integrity, truncation enforcement, reduction replay, loss metric replay,
invariant check replay, and interop claim consistency. It fixed acceptance rules and required
failure codes, making reducers replayable and registry-grade.

publish interop certificates for bucketed workflows.

6 Certificate and Verifier: Reduction Replay, Loss Accounting,
and Invariant Acceptance

6.1 Purpose

EY29 reductions are used as registry keys, bucket labels, and verifier-friendly summaries. There-
fore, a reducer must publish:

• the full reducer SpecID (including ReducerCore parameters),
• deterministic transcripts that allow replay,
• invariant check results (per InvPolicy),
• loss metrics (per LossSpec),
• and failure codes when reduction cannot be accepted.

This chapter specifies:
• the certificate payload πCGR,
• deterministic verifier checks for acceptance,
• transcript commitments for reduction computations,
• and required failure codes.

6.2 Certificate Object πCGR

Rule. An EY29 publication MUST include a certificate πCGR in canonical certificate encoding
(EY22-CCE).

739



Header (required)

• artifact type: CGR

• artifact symbol: R
• RedClass, NMap, InputType, OutputType
• Version
• Certificate schema identifier (EY22-CCE)

SpecID (required)

The full SpecID tuple MUST be embedded:

SpecIDEY29 := (CGR, InputType, OutputType, ReducerSpec, TruncSpec, NumericModel, TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version).

Committed Inputs (required)

πCGR MUST commit to:
• ReducerSpec including ReducerCore (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold),
• TruncSpec including Nin, Nout and any CrossNPolicy rules,
• NumericModel (including ordering/canonicalization),
• InvPolicy (names, statuses, tolerances, check routines),
• LossSpec (definitions, routines, tolerances or explicit null),
• any external referenced objects used by invariant checks (e.g. EY27 PredID, EY24 validity,

EY28 bridge transcripts),
• input object commitment hA (or a reference to the upstream artifact output hash).

Committed Outputs (required)

πCGR MUST commit to:
• reduced output object Ã (or its hash) and canonical encoding rule,
• reduction transcript commitment Txcgr,
• invariant report commitment Txinv,
• loss report commitment Txloss,
• deterministic failure code if reduction or checks fail.

6.3 Reduction Transcript (Minimum Contents)

The reduction transcript MUST bind enough information to replay:
• input hash hA and any upstream references (artifact IDs, output hashes),
• reducer core resolution (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold) and their hashes,
• truncation mapping decisions (including rounding/tie-breaks and CrossNPolicy outputs),

740



• deterministic scan orders (block order, entry order, reduction order),
• canonicalization points and rules,
• reduced output hash h (or hash of bucket+summary encoding).

Ã

Rule (registry-grade output). If Ã or BucketID is used as a registry key, πCGR MUST
include:

• a stable canonical encoding of the key material,
• and the exact CrossNPolicy (if any) that produced it.

6.4 Invariant Report (Required Structure)

An invariant report is the canonical serialization of:

InvReport := {(InvName,Status,Result,Value,Tol)}.

Rule. For Status = discarded, Result, Value, Tol MUST be null. For preserved/weakened
invariants, they MUST be non-null.

6.5 Loss Report (Required Structure)

A loss report is the canonical serialization of:

LossReport := {(LossName,Value,Tol)}.

Rule. If a loss metric is declared but not computed, Value MUST be null, and the verifier
must check that the SpecID justification exists. Otherwise: FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED.

6.6 Verifier Contract

A verifier consumes πCGR and returns:

{ACCEPT,REJECT} ∪ {FAIL_∗}.

Acceptance meaning. ACCEPT means: the reducer artifact is well-formed, replayable, the
reduced output matches replay, loss metrics are computed as declared, and invariants marked
preserved/weakened satisfy their check rules within tolerance. It does not imply any invariant
marked discarded, and it does not imply preservation beyond InvPolicy.

6.7 Required Verifier Checks (Normative)

V1: Structural Validity (EY22-CCE)

Parse canonical certificate encoding and confirm required fields exist. Failure: REJECT_MALFORMED.

741



V2: SpecID Completeness

Confirm:
• ArtifactType=CGR,
• InputType, OutputType,
• ReducerSpec (RedClass, NMap, ReducerCore, InvPolicy, LossSpec),
• TruncSpec, NumericModel,
• TranscriptSpec, Cert, Interop, Version.

Failure: REJECT_SPECID_MISSING, REJECT_REDCLASS_MISSING, RE-
JECT_NMAP_MISSING, REJECT_INVPOLICY_MISSING.

V3: Commitment Integrity

Verify all hash-committed objects resolve and match:
• reducer core components (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold),
• input commitment hA (or upstream output hash),
• any referenced external artifacts used by invariant checks (PredIDs, validity objects),
• transcript commitments.

Failure: FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH, REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT.

V4: Truncation and NMap Enforcement

Enforce NMap and TruncSpec:
• same-N : check Nin = Nout,
• shrink-N : recompute declared mapping and rounding,
• multi-N : verify lists and CrossNPolicy selection (if used).

Failure: FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH.

V5: Reduction Replay

Replay reduction deterministically:
• run CGR-R0 preparation,
• run the declared reduction routine for RedClass (CGR-R1..R5) and CGR-R8 if multi-N ,
• apply declared scan orders and canonicalization points.

Compare the replayed reduced output hash to published h (or bucket+summary encoding
Ã

hash). Failure: FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH, FAIL_NONDETERMINISM,
FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH.

742



V6: Loss Metric Replay

Replay all loss metrics in LossSpec via CGR-R7. Compare to published LossReport. Failure:
FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED, FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

V7: Invariant Check Replay

Replay all preserved/weakened invariants via CGR-R6, including any referenced EY27/EY24/EY28
routines. Compare to published InvReport. Failure: FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED,
FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE, FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH.

V8: Interop Claim Consistency

If Interop claims composition with other artifacts:
• verify referenced artifacts (by hash/SpecID) exist and match,
• verify that invariants required by those workflows are not marked discarded in InvPolicy,
• verify that BUCK outputs used as keys include CrossNPolicy and stability diagnostics if

declared.
Failure: FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE.

6.8 Acceptance Rule

Rule. A verifier returns ACCEPT iff:
• V1–V5 pass,
• LossReport matches replayed loss metrics for all declared metrics,
• InvReport matches replayed invariant checks for all preserved/weakened invariants,
• transcript commitments match.

If an invariant marked preserved fails, return FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED
(not ACCEPT).

6.9 Required Failure Codes

At minimum:
• REJECT_MALFORMED
• REJECT_SPECID_MISSING
• REJECT_REDCLASS_MISSING
• REJECT_NMAP_MISSING
• REJECT_INVPOLICY_MISSING
• REJECT_HIDDEN_INPUT
• FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH
• FAIL_TRUNC_MISMATCH

743



• FAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH
• FAIL_NONDETERMINISM
• FAIL_TRANSCRIPT_MISMATCH
• FAIL_LOSS_UNDEFINED
• FAIL_INVARIANT_NOT_PRESERVED
• FAIL_COMPAT_PREDICATE

6.10 Chapter Summary

This chapter defined the EY29 certificate πCGR and deterministic verifier checks: SpecID
completeness, commitment integrity, truncation enforcement, reduction replay, loss metric replay,
invariant check replay, and interop claim consistency. It fixed acceptance rules and required
failure codes, making reducers replayable and registry-grade.

7 CGR-0 Reference Instance, Publication Boundary, and Non-
Claims

7.1 Purpose

This chapter closes EY29 by:
• providing a concrete CGR-0 reference SpecID template (a stable meaning of “coarse-grain

reducer artifact”),
• fixing what must be published for a valid EY29 reducer,
• stating explicit non-claims (what reduction does not guarantee),
• and recording licensing intent consistent with Vol. No. IV.

7.2 CGR-0 Reference Instance (Template)

CGR-0 is the conservative baseline profile defined in Chapter 4. The following template fixes a
“default” reducer SpecID for universal verifiers.

CGR-0 profile choices.
• RedClass ∈ {PROJ,AGG,BUCK},
• NMap ∈ {same-N, shrink-N} (multi-N is non-baseline),
• deterministic reducer core commitments (projector/partition/classifier),
• mandatory loss metrics: ∥A− Ã∥F for PROJ/AGG, and stability/margin diagnostics for

BUCK,
• InvPolicy must include I1 (Domain) and I8 (Replay), and any workflow-dependent invariants

(I6/I7) MUST NOT be discarded.

7.3 Publication Boundary (Normative)

Rule (what must be public). An EY29 publication MUST include:
• full SpecIDEY29,
• ReducerCore commitments (projector/partition/classifier/seed/threshold) sufficient to

replay,
• TruncSpec and NMap decisions (including rounding/tie-breaks),
• NumericModel (including ordering/canonicalization),
• InvPolicy and CheckRoutineIDs for all preserved/weakened invariants,
• LossSpec and RoutineIDs for all declared loss metrics (or explicit null-justifications),

746



• certificate πCGR with transcript commitments, invariant report, and loss report,
• deterministic failure codes (or PASS) for all declared checks.

Rule (no hidden classifier). If RedClass=BUCK, the classifier rules (bucket boundaries,
feature definitions, and tie-breaks) MUST be committed by hash or explicit encoding. A bucket
label without classifier commitments is invalid.

Rule (no hidden partition). If RedClass=AGG, the partition must be public (explicit list,
committed hash, or seed+generator). Averaging across hidden blocks is invalid.

7.4 Non-Claims (Explicit)

EY29 explicitly does not claim:

NC1: Truth Preservation Beyond Declared InvPolicy

Reduction is not assumed to preserve any property not listed in InvPolicy. In particular,
commutation, validity, positivity, and spectral class are not preserved unless explicitly declared
and checked.

NC2: Infinite-Dimensional Guarantees

Passing reduction checks at finite truncations does not imply anything about the infinite-
dimensional limit. No analytic equivalence is implied by a stable bucket label.

NC3: Uniqueness of the Reduction

Multiple reducers may map the same A to different reduced objects. EY29 does not claim
uniqueness; it binds this reducer instance by SpecID.

NC4: Adversarial Robustness Beyond Verifier Checks

EY29 reduces smuggling by commitment and replay, but does not guarantee robustness against
adversarial feature engineering beyond declared checks.

NC5: Cross-Workflow Comparability Without Shared SpecID

Reduced outputs are comparable only when reducer SpecIDs match (or a declared coercion
exists). A bucket label from a different classifier is a different object.

7.5 Licensing Intent (Vol. No. IV)

The EY29 specification (schemas, baseline routines, invariant vocabulary, verifier checks) is
intended to remain publicly readable. Implementations and classifier catalogs may be licensed
under project-chosen terms, but:

loss accounting and replayability may not be removed.

747



Rule (no audit stripping). No distribution or license arrangement may claim EY29 compli-
ance while omitting:

• reducer core commitments,
• loss reports,
• invariant reports,
• and verifier replay rules.

7.6 Chapter Summary

This chapter provided a CGR-0 reference SpecID template, fixed the EY29 publication boundary
(what must be committed and public), stated explicit non-claims (no implied preservation beyond
InvPolicy, no infinite-limit guarantees, no uniqueness, no extra robustness, no comparability
without shared SpecID), and recorded licensing intent consistent with Vol. No. IV: the spec
remains auditable and public; implementations may vary, but replayability and loss accounting
are mandatory.

from state/operator workflows into observable-space dynamics, and binds how Vol. No. IV
artifacts can be exported into Koopman form with interop and verification.

8 Worked Examples (Non-Normative): Reduction Patterns for
Vol. No. IV

8.1 Purpose

This chapter is non-normative. It illustrates typical EY29 usage patterns:
• projecting onto a low-frequency subspace (PROJ),
• aggregating an operator into block form (AGG),
• producing bucket labels and summaries (BUCK) for registries,
• treating regime transport as reduction when N shrinks (INTW → CGR),
• and exporting reduced summaries into Koopman workflows (CGR → KOOP).

Reminder. Examples become valid only when reducer core parameters, truncation mapping,
invariants, and loss metrics are fully committed and replayable.

8.2 Example 1: PROJ — Low-Mode Projection of a Filtered Hamiltonian

Goal. Reduce a filtered operator to its low-mode subspace:

H̃ := P F⋆(H)P,

with P selecting the lowest Nout basis modes.

748



ReducerSpec sketch.
• RedClass=PROJ, NMap=shrink-N
• ProjType=basis-prefix, selection rule: “first Nout modes”
• Loss metric: ∥F⋆(H)− H̃∥F
• Invariants:

– I1 (Domain) preserved,
– I5 (Norm Bound) weakened with tolerance,
– I2 (Spectrum) weakened (spectral summary computed only on low block).

Interpretation. The reduced operator is not claimed to reproduce high-frequency spectral
details; the loss metric explicitly quantifies discarded content.

8.3 Example 2: AGG — Block-Coarse Operator for Compatibility Matrices

Goal. Partition the basis into m blocks and aggregate:
1 ∑ ∑

Ãij := A
|Bi||

pq.
Bj | p∈Bi q∈Bj

Use case. A compatibility matrix entry may require a small operator (e.g. m ≤ 32) that can
be replayed quickly by many verifiers.

ReducerSpec sketch.
• RedClass=AGG, NMap=same-N (output is m×m)
• PartitionSpec committed by hash (explicit block list)
• Aggregation Φ=mean, with deterministic reduction order
• Loss metrics:

– ∥A− Â∥F where Â is the lifted block operator,
– within-block variance (stability diagnostic).

Interpretation. AGG produces a coarse operator that is meaningful only under the declared
partition. Without that partition commitment, the summary is meaningless.

8.4 Example 3: BUCK — Registry Key for “Spectral Class”

Goal. Produce a stable bucket label and a bounded summary:
R(A) := (BucketID(A), s(A)).

Typical inputs.
• A = F⋆(H) (output of EY23),
• A = V (validity object from EY24),
• or a token-derived object from EY26.

749



Multi-N stability (optional). Compute labels across Nin and aggregate with CrossNPol-
icy=stable-first: choose the first N where label stabilizes and record the stabilization index
as diagnostic.

Loss metrics.
• bucket margin (distance to decision boundary),
• stability score across truncations.

Interpretation. BUCK makes registry-grade keys possible, but only because the classifier and
features are committed and replayable.

8.5 Example 4: INTW → CGR — Transport as Reduction

Goal. Bridge from regime 1 to regime 2 and shrink N :
H2 := TH1S, H̃2 := R(H2), Nout < Nin.

Two equivalent-looking orders (not equivalent).
• Order A: transport then reduce,
• Order B: reduce then transport.

Rule reminder. The workflow MUST declare the order (EY29 Chapter ??). The order affects
loss accounting and invariants.

Interop certificate must bind.
• EY28 πINTW reference,
• EY29 πCGR reference,
• the order and scope (which object was transported/reduced),
• combined truncation policy and deterministic tie-breaks.

8.6 Example 5: CGR → KOOP — Reduced Summaries for Koopman Export

Goal. Export a reduced observable basis into Koopman form:
(BucketID, s) := R(trajectory summary), K(g) acts on the reduced observable set.

Interpretation. Koopman export becomes feasible for many verifiers when the observable
basis and summaries are bounded and replayable. CGR binds which details were discarded and
how much was lost.

8.7 Example 6: Reduction Under Constraints (EY27 + EY29)

Goal. Reduce A and B while tracking commutation weakening:
δcomm := ∥[A,B]∥, δ̃comm := ∥[Ã, B̃]∥.

750



Policy choices.
• preserve: require δ̃comm ≤ ε (strict),
• weaken: require δ̃comm ≤ g(δcomm) for a declared function g,
• discard: allowed only if the workflow explicitly does not rely on the constraint.

Interpretation. Reduction is not allowed to silently break constraints if the workflow depends
on them.

8.8 Chapter Summary

This non-normative chapter illustrated EY29 in common Vol. No. IV workflows: PROJ low-mode
projection, AGG block-aggregation for small verifier-friendly operators, BUCK bucket labels +
summaries for registries, INTW-as-reduction when truncation shrinks across regimes, reduction
feeding Koopman export, and reduction under commutation constraints.
